action.name: Attack
entries: When you take the Attack action, you can make one attack roll with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|srd52}.

entries.name: Equipping and Unequipping Weapons
entries: You can either equip or unequip one weapon when you make an attack as part of this action. You do so either before or after the attack. If you equip a weapon before an attack, you don't need to use it for that attack. Equipping a weapon includes drawing it from a sheath or picking it up. Unequipping a weapon includes sheathing, stowing, or dropping it.

entries.name: Moving Between Attacks
entries: If you move on your turn and have a feature, such as Extra Attack, that gives you more than one attack as part of the Attack action, you can use some or all of that movement to move between those attacks.

action.name: Dash
entries: When you take the Dash action, you gain extra movement for the current turn. The increase equals your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} after applying any modifiers. With a {@variantrule Speed|srd52} of 30 feet, for example, you can move up to 60 feet on your turn if you Dash. If your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} of 30 feet is reduced to 15 feet, you can move up to 30 feet this turn if you Dash.

If you have a special speed, such as a {@variantrule Fly Speed|srd52} or {@variantrule Swim Speed|srd52}, you can use that speed instead of your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} when you take this action. You choose which speed to use each time you take it.

action.name: Disengage
entries: If you take the Disengage action, your movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|srd52|Opportunity Attacks} for the rest of the current turn.

action.name: Dodge
entries: If you take the Dodge action, you gain the following benefits: until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against you has {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throws} with {@variantrule Advantage|srd52}.
You lose these benefits if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} condition or if your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} is 0.

action.name: Don or Doff a Shield
entries: A {@item Shield|srd52} can be donned or doffed as an action.

action.name: End Concentration
entries: Some spells and other effects require Concentration to remain active, as specified in their descriptions. You can end Concentration at any time (no action required).

action.name: Escape a Grapple
entries: A Grappled creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|srd52}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|srd52}) check against the grapple's escape DC, ending the {@variantrule Condition|srd52|condition} on itself on a success. The {@variantrule Condition|srd52|condition} also ends if the grappler has the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} condition or if the distance between the Grappled target and the grappler exceeds the grapple's range.

action.name: Help
entries: When you take the Help action, you do one of the following.

entries.name: Assist an Ability Check
entries: Choose one of your skill or tool proficiencies and one ally who is near enough for you to assist verbally or physically when they make an ability check. That ally has {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} on the next ability check they make with the chosen skill or tool. This benefit expires if the ally doesn't use it before the start of your next turn. The GM has final say on whether your assistance is possible.

entries.name: Assist an Attack Roll
entries: You momentarily distract an enemy within 5 feet of you, giving {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} to the next attack roll by one of your allies against that enemy. This benefit expires at the start of your next turn.
{@note Additionally, the Help action may be used to {@book stabilize a creature|srd52|1|Stabilizing a Character}.}

action.name: Hide
entries: With the Hide action, you try to conceal yourself. To do so, you must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|srd52}) check while you're {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|srd52} or behind {@variantrule Cover|srd52|Three-Quarters Cover or Total Cover}, and you must be out of any enemy's line of sight; if you can see a creature, you can discern whether it can see you.

On a successful check, you have the {@condition Invisible|srd52} condition while hidden. Make note of your check's total, which is the DC for a creature to find you with a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|srd52}) check.
You stop being hidden immediately after any of the following occurs: you make a sound louder than a whisper, an enemy finds you, you make an attack roll, or you cast a spell with a Verbal component.

action.name: Influence
entries: With the Influence action, you urge a monster to do something. Describe or roleplay how you're communicating with the monster. Are you trying to deceive, intimidate, amuse, or gently persuade? The GM then determines whether the monster feels willing, unwilling, or hesitant due to your interaction; this determination establishes whether an ability check is necessary, as explained below.

entries.name: Willing
entries: If your urging aligns with the monster's desires, no ability check is necessary; the monster fulfills your request in a way it prefers.

entries.name: Unwilling
entries: If your urging is repugnant to the monster or counter to its alignment, no ability check is necessary; it doesn't comply.

entries.name: Hesitant
entries: If you urge the monster to do something that it is hesitant to do, you must make an ability check, which is affected by the monster's attitude: Indifferent, Friendly, or Hostile, each of which is defined in this glossary. The Influence Checks table suggests which ability check to make based on how you're interacting with the monster. The GM chooses the check, which has a default DC equal to 15 or the monster's Intelligence score, whichever is higher. On a successful check, the monster does as urged. On a failed check, you must wait 24 hours (or a duration set by the DM) before urging it in the same way again.

entries.caption: Influence Checks
rows: Deceiving a monster that understands you
Persuading a monster that understands you
Gently coaxing a Beast or Monstrosity

action.name: Magic
entries: When you take the {@action Magic|srd52} action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a {@action Magic|srd52} action to be activated.

If you cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 minute or longer, you must take the {@action Magic|srd52} action on each turn of that casting, and you must maintain {@status Concentration|srd52} while you do so. If your {@status Concentration|srd52} is broken, the spell fails, but you don't expend a spell slot.

action.name: Opportunity Attack
entries: You can make an Opportunity Attack when a creature that you can see leaves your reach using its action, its {@variantrule Bonus Action|srd52}, its {@variantrule Reaction|srd52}, or one of its speeds. To make the Opportunity Attack, take a {@variantrule Reaction|srd52} to make one melee attack with a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|srd52} against the provoking creature. The attack occurs right before the creature leaves your reach.

action.name: Ready
entries: You take the Ready action to wait for a particular circumstance before you act. To do so, you take this action on your turn, which lets you act by taking a {@variantrule Reaction|srd52} before the start of your next turn.

First, you decide what perceivable circumstance will trigger your {@variantrule Reaction|srd52}. Then, you choose the action you will take in response to that trigger, or you choose to move up to your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} in response to it. Examples include "If the cultist steps on the trapdoor, I'll pull the lever that opens it," and "If the zombie steps next to me, I move away."
When the trigger occurs, you can either take your {@variantrule Reaction|srd52} right after the trigger finishes or ignore the trigger.

When you Ready a spell, you cast it as normal (expending any resources used to cast it) but hold its energy, which you release with your {@variantrule Reaction|srd52} when the trigger occurs. To be readied, a spell must have a casting time of an action, and holding on to the spell's magic requires {@status Concentration|srd52}, which you can maintain up to the start of your next turn. If your {@status Concentration|srd52} is broken, the spell dissipates without taking effect.

action.name: Search
entries: When you take the Search action, you make a Wisdom check to discern something that isn't obvious. The Search table suggests which skills are applicable when you take this action, depending on what you're trying to detect.

entries.caption: Search
rows: Creature's ailment or cause of death

action.name: Study
entries: When you take the Study action, you make an Intelligence check to study your memory, a book, a clue, or another source of knowledge and call to mind an important piece of information about it.
The Areas of Knowledge table suggests which skills are applicable to various areas of knowledge.

entries.caption: Areas of Knowledge
rows: Spells, magic items, eldritch symbols, magical traditions, planes of existence, and certain creatures (Aberrations, Constructs, Elementals, Fey, and Monstrosities)
Historic events and people, ancient civilizations, wars, and certain creatures (Giants and Humanoids)
Terrain, flora, weather, and certain creatures (Beasts, Dragons, Oozes, and Plants)
Deities, religious hierarchies and rites, holy symbols, cults, and certain creatures (Celestials, Fiends, and Undead)

action.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|srd52} action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|srd52} later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a different Light weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative. For example, you can attack with a {@item Shortsword|srd52} in one hand and a {@item Dagger|srd52} in the other using the {@action Attack|srd52} action and a {@variantrule Bonus Action|srd52}, but you don't add your Strength or Dexterity modifier to the damage roll of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|srd52} unless that modifier is negative.

action.name: Utilize
entries: You normally interact with an object while doing something else, such as when you draw a sword as part of the {@action Attack|srd52} action. When an object requires an action for its use, you take the Utilize action.

classFeature.name: Rage
entries: You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52} if you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

You can enter your Rage the number of times shown for your Barbarian level in the Rages column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
While active, your Rage follows the rules below.

entries.name: Damage Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

entries.name: Rage Damage
entries: When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52}—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

entries.name: Strength Advantage
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

entries.name: No Concentration or Spells
entries: You can't maintain {@status Concentration|SRD52}, and you can't cast spells.

entries.name: Duration
entries: The Rage lasts until the end of your next turn, and it ends early if you don Heavy armor or have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition. If your Rage is still active on your next turn, you can extend the Rage for another round by doing one of the following:

items: Make an attack roll against an enemy.
Force an enemy to make a saving throw.
Take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52} to extend your Rage.

entries: Each time the Rage is extended, it lasts until the end of your next turn. You can maintain a Rage for up to 10 minutes.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While you aren't wearing any armor, your base {@variantrule Armor Class|SRD52} equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a {@item Shield|SRD52} and still gain this benefit.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of two kinds of {@filter Simple|items|type=simple weapon;melee weapon=sand} or {@filter Martial Melee weapons|items|type=martial weapon;melee weapon=sand} of your choice, such as {@item Greataxe|SRD52|Greataxes} and {@item Handaxe|SRD52|Handaxes}. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Barbarian levels, you gain the ability to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Barbarian Features table.

classFeature.name: Danger Sense
entries: You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition.

classFeature.name: Reckless Attack
entries: You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on attack rolls using Strength until the start of your next turn, but attack rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} during that time.

classFeature.name: Barbarian Subclass
entries: You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Barbarian level or lower.

classFeature.name: Primal Knowledge
entries: You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1.

In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: {@skill Acrobatics|SRD52}, {@skill Intimidation|SRD52}, {@skill Perception|SRD52}, {@skill Stealth|SRD52}, or {@skill Survival|SRD52}. When you use this ability, your Strength represents primal power coursing through you, honing your agility, bearing, and senses.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Fast Movement
entries: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Barbarian subclass.

classFeature.name: Feral Instinct
entries: Your instincts are so honed that you have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52} rolls.

classFeature.name: Instinctive Pounce
entries: As part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52} you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Brutal Strike
entries: If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|SRD52}. If the chosen attack roll hits, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} damage of the same type dealt by the weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52}, and you can cause one Brutal Strike effect of your choice. You have the following effect options.

entries.name: Forceful Blow
entries: The target is pushed 15 feet straight away from you. You can then move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|SRD52} straight toward the target without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|SRD52|Opportunity Attacks}.

entries.name: Hamstring Blow
entries: The target's {@variantrule Speed|SRD52} is reduced by 15 feet until the start of your next turn. A target can be affected by only one Hamstring Blow at a time—the most recent one.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Barbarian subclass.

classFeature.name: Relentless Rage
entries: Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} while your Rage is active and don't die outright, you can make a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, your {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} instead change to a number equal to twice your Barbarian level.
Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, the DC resets to 10.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Improved Brutal Strike
entries: You have honed new ways to attack furiously. The following effects are now among your Brutal Strike options.

entries.name: Staggering Blow
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|SRD52} on the next saving throw it makes, and it can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|SRD52|Opportunity Attacks} until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Sundering Blow
entries: Before the start of your next turn, the next attack roll made by another creature against the target gains a +5 bonus to the roll. An attack roll can gain only one Sundering Blow bonus.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Barbarian subclass.

classFeature.name: Persistent Rage
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52}, you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

In addition, your Rage is so fierce that it now lasts for 10 minutes without you needing to do anything to extend it from round to round. Your Rage ends early if you have the {@condition Unconscious|SRD52} condition (not just the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition) or don Heavy armor.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Improved Brutal Strike
entries: The extra damage of your Brutal Strike increases to {@damage 2d10}. In addition, you can use two different Brutal Strike effects whenever you use your Brutal Strike feature.

classFeature.name: Indomitable Might
entries: If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Irresistible Offense|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Primal Champion
entries: You embody primal power. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

classFeature.name: Bardic Inspiration
entries: You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which is a {@dice d6}.

entries.name: Using Bardic Inspiration
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can inspire another creature within 60 feet of yourself who can see or hear you. That creature gains one of your Bardic Inspiration dice. A creature can have only one Bardic Inspiration die at a time.

Once within the next hour when the creature fails a {@variantrule D20 Test|SRD52}, the creature can roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to the {@dice d20}, potentially turning the failure into a success. A Bardic Inspiration die is expended when it's rolled.

entries.name: Number of Uses
entries: You can confer a Bardic Inspiration die a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: Your Bardic Inspiration die changes when you reach certain Bard levels, as shown in the Bardic Die column of the Bard Features table. The die becomes a {@dice d8} at level 5, a {@dice d10} at level 10, and a {@dice d12} at level 15.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts. See {@book chapter 7|SRD52|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Bard spells, which appear in the {@filter Bard spell list|spells|class=Bard} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Bard spell list|spells|class=Bard}. {@spell Dancing Lights|SRD52} and {@spell Vicious Mockery|SRD52} are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Bard spell list|spells|class=Bard}.
When you reach Bard levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Bard spell list|spells|class=Bard}, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Bard Features table.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Bard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the {@filter Bard spell list|spells|class=Bard}. {@spell Charm Person|SRD52}, {@spell Color Spray|SRD52}, {@spell Dissonant Whispers|SRD52}, and {@spell Healing Word|SRD52} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Bard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Bard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the {@filter Bard spell list|spells|class=Bard} until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Bard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Bard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Bard spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Bard level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Bard spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Bard spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use a {@item Musical Instrument|SRD52} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|SRD52} for your Bard spells.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. {@skill Performance|SRD52} and {@skill Persuasion|SRD52} are recommended if you have proficiency in them.
At Bard level 9, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

classFeature.name: Jack of All Trades
entries: You can add half your {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus} (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn't otherwise use your {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus}.

For example, if you make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|SRD52}) check and lack {@skill Athletics|SRD52} proficiency, you can add half your {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus} to the check.

entries.name: A Bard's Repertoire
entries: Does your Bard beat a {@item drum|SRD52} while chanting the deeds of ancient heroes? Strum a {@item lute|SRD52} while crooning romantic tunes? Perform arias of stirring power? Recite dramatic monologues from classic tragedies? Use the rhythm of a folk dance to coordinate the movement of allies in battle? Compose naughty limericks?

When you play a Bard, consider the style of artistic performance you favor, the moods you might invoke, and the themes that inspire your own creations. Are your poems inspired by moments of natural beauty, or are they brooding reflections on loss? Do you prefer lofty hymns or rowdy tavern songs? Are you drawn to laments for the fallen or celebrations of joy? Do you dance merry jigs or perform elaborate interpretive choreography? Do you focus on one style of performance or strive to master them all?

classFeature.name: Bard Subclass
entries: You gain a Bard subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Bard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Bard level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Bard levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Font of Inspiration
entries: You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Bard Subclass.

classFeature.name: Countercharm
entries: You can use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the {@condition Charmed|SRD52} or {@condition Frightened|SRD52} condition, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|SRD52} to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in two of your Skill Proficiencies of your choice.

classFeature.name: Magical Secrets
entries: You've learned secrets from various magical traditions. Whenever you reach a Bard level (including this level) and the Prepared Spells number in the Bard Features table increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells from the {@filter Bard|spells|class=Bard}, {@filter Cleric|spells|class=Cleric}, {@filter Druid|spells|class=Druid}, and {@filter Wizard|spells|class=Wizard} {@filter spell lists|spells|class=Bard;Cleric;Druid;Wizard}, and the chosen spells count as Bard spells for you (see a class's section for its spell list). In addition, whenever you replace a spell prepared for this class, you can replace it with a spell from those lists.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Bard Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Superior Inspiration
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52}, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Spell Recall|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Words of Creation
entries: You have mastered two of the Words of Creation: the words of life and death. You therefore always have the {@spell Power Word Heal|SRD52} and {@spell Power Word Kill|SRD52} spells prepared. When you cast either spell, you can target a second creature with it if that creature is within 10 feet of the first target.

classFeature.name: Divine Order
entries: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

classFeature.name: Protector
entries: Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} and training with {@filter Heavy armor|items|type=Heavy Armor}.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See {@book chapter 7|SRD52|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Cleric spells, which appear on the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know three cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric}. {@spell Guidance|SRD52}, {@spell Sacred Flame|SRD52}, and {@spell Thaumaturgy|SRD52} are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Cleric level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric}.
When you reach Cleric levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric}, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Cleric Features table.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Cleric Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric}. {@spell Bless|SRD52}, {@spell Cure Wounds|SRD52}, {@spell Guiding Bolt|SRD52}, and {@spell Shield of Faith|SRD52} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Cleric levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Cleric Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric} until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Cleric, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Cleric feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Cleric spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Cleric spells for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Cleric spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use a {@item Holy Symbol|SRD52} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|SRD52} for your Cleric spells.

classFeature.name: Thaumaturge
entries: You know one extra cantrip from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric}. In addition, your mystical connection to the divine gives you a bonus to your Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|SRD52} or {@skill Religion|SRD52}) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

classFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Divine Spark and Turn Undead, each of which is described below. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, choose which Channel Divinity effect from this class to create. You gain additional effect options at higher Cleric levels.

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. You gain additional uses when you reach certain Cleric levels, as shown in the Channel Divinity column of the Cleric Features table.
If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

classFeature.name: Divine Spark
entries: As a {@action Magic|SRD52} action, you point your {@item Holy Symbol|SRD52} at another creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself and focus divine energy at it. Roll {@dice 1d8} and add your Wisdom modifier. You either restore {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} to the creature equal to that total or force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to that total. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage (round down).
You roll an additional {@dice d8} when you reach Cleric levels 7 ({@dice 2d8}), 13 ({@dice 3d8}), and 18 ({@dice 4d8}).

classFeature.name: Turn Undead
entries: As a {@action Magic|SRD52} action, you present your {@item Holy Symbol|SRD52} and censure Undead creatures. Each Undead of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its save, it has the {@condition Frightened|SRD52} and {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} conditions for 1 minute. For that duration, it tries to move as far from you as it can on its turns. This effect ends early on the creature if it takes any damage, if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition, or if you die.

classFeature.name: Cleric Subclass
entries: You gain a Cleric subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Cleric levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Cleric level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Sear Undead
entries: Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of {@dice 1d8}) and add the rolls together. Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll's total. This damage doesn't end the turn effect.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Cleric Subclass.

classFeature.name: Blessed Strikes
entries: Divine power infuses you in battle. You gain one of the following options of your choice (if you get either option from a Cleric subclass in an older book, use only the option you choose for this feature).

classFeature.name: Divine Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can cause the target to take an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice).

classFeature.name: Potent Spellcasting
entries: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Cleric cantrip.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Divine Intervention
entries: You can call on your deity or pantheon to intervene on your behalf. As a {@action Magic|SRD52} action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn't require a {@variantrule Reaction|SRD52} to cast. As part of the same action, you cast that spell without expending a spell slot or needing Material components. You can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Improved Blessed Strikes
entries: The option you chose for Blessed Strikes grows more powerful.

entries.name: Divine Strike
entries: The extra damage of your Divine Strike increases to {@damage 2d8}.

entries.name: Potent Spellcasting
entries: When you cast a Cleric cantrip and deal damage to a creature with it, you can give vitality to yourself or another creature within 60 feet of yourself, granting a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|SRD52} equal to twice your Wisdom modifier.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Cleric Subclass.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Fate|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Greater Divine Intervention
entries: You can call on even more powerful divine intervention. When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose {@spell Wish|SRD52} when you select a spell. If you do so, you can't use Divine Intervention again until you finish {@dice 2d4} Long Rests.

classFeature.name: Druidic
entries: You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the {@spell Speak with Animals|SRD52} spell prepared.

You can use Druidic to leave hidden messages. You and others who know Druidic automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|SRD52}) check but can't decipher it without magic.

classFeature.name: Magician
entries: You know one extra cantrip from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}. In addition, your mystical connection to nature gives you a bonus to your Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|SRD52} or {@skill Nature|SRD52}) checks. The bonus equals your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

classFeature.name: Primal Order
entries: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. See {@book chapter 7|SRD52|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Druid spells, which appear on the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}. {@spell Druidcraft|SRD52} and {@spell Produce Flame|SRD52} are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Druid level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}.
When you reach Druid levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Druid Features table.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid}. {@spell Animal Friendship|SRD52}, {@spell Cure Wounds|SRD52}, {@spell Faerie Fire|SRD52}, and {@spell Thunderwave|SRD52} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Druid levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Druid Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the {@filter Druid spell list|spells|class=Druid} until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Druid, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Druid feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Druid spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells with other Druid spells for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Druid spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use a {@item Druidic Focus|SRD52} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|SRD52} for your Druid spells.

classFeature.name: Warden
entries: Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with {@filter Martial weapons|items|type=martial weapon} and training with {@filter Medium armor|items|type=Medium Armor}.

classFeature.name: Wild Companion
entries: You can summon a nature spirit that assumes an animal form to aid you. As a {@action Magic|SRD52} action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the {@spell Find Familiar|SRD52} spell without Material components.
When you cast the spell in this way, the familiar is Fey and disappears when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Wild Shape
entries: The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see "Known Forms" below). You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}.

entries.name: Number of Uses
entries: You can use Wild Shape twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
You gain additional uses when you reach certain Druid levels, as shown in the Wild Shape column of the Druid Features table.

entries.name: Known Forms
entries: You know four Beast forms for this feature, chosen from among Beast stat blocks that have a maximum {@variantrule Challenge Rating|SRD52} of 1/4 and that lack a {@variantrule Fly Speed|SRD52} (see appendix B for stat block options). The {@creature Rat|SRD52}, {@creature Riding Horse|SRD52}, {@creature Spider|SRD52}, and {@creature Wolf|SRD52} are recommended. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can replace one of your known forms with another eligible form.

When you reach certain Druid levels, your number of known forms and the maximum {@variantrule Challenge Rating|SRD52} for those forms increases, as shown in the Beast Shapes table. In addition, starting at level 8, you can adopt a form that has a {@variantrule Fly Speed|SRD52}.
When choosing known forms, you may look in the {@book Monster Manual|SRD52} or elsewhere for eligible Beasts if the Dungeon Master permits you to do so.

entries.name: Rules While Shape-Shifted
entries: While in a form, you retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak, and the following rules apply:

items.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|SRD52} equal to your Druid level.

items.name: Game Statistics
entries: Your game statistics are replaced by the Beast's stat block, but you retain your creature type; {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52}; {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|SRD52}; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies and use your {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus} for them, in addition to gaining the proficiencies of the creature. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block.

items.name: No Spellcasting
entries: You can't cast spells, but shape-shifting doesn't break your {@status Concentration|SRD52} or otherwise interfere with a spell you've already cast.

items.name: Objects
entries: Your ability to handle objects is determined by the form's limbs rather than your own. In addition, you choose whether your equipment falls in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it's practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment based on the creature's size and shape. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with the form. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect while you're in that form.

classFeature.name: Druid Subclass
entries: You gain a Druid subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Druid levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Druid level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Druid levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Wild Resurgence
entries: Once on each of your turns, if you have no uses of Wild Shape left, you can give yourself one use by expending a spell slot (no action required).
In addition, you can expend one use of Wild Shape (no action required) to give yourself a level 1 spell slot, but you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Druid Subclass.

classFeature.name: Elemental Fury
entries: The might of the elements flows through you. You gain one of the following options of your choice.

classFeature.name: Potent Spellcasting
entries: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Druid cantrip.

classFeature.name: Primal Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or a Beast form's attack in Wild Shape, you can cause the target to take an extra {@damage 1d8} Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage (choose when you hit).

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Druid Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Druid Subclass.

classFeature.name: Improved Elemental Fury
entries: The option you chose for Elemental Fury grows more powerful, as detailed below.

entries.name: Potent Spellcasting
entries: When you cast a Druid cantrip with a range of 10 feet or greater, the spell's range increases by 300 feet.

entries.name: Primal Strike
entries: The extra damage of your Primal Strike increases to {@damage 2d8}.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Beast Spells
entries: While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Dimensional Travel|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Archdruid
entries: The vitality of nature constantly blooms within you, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Evergreen Wild Shape
entries: Whenever you roll {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52} and have no uses of Wild Shape left, you regain one expended use of it.

entries.name: Nature Magician
entries: You can convert uses of Wild Shape into a spell slot (no action required). Choose a number of your unexpended uses of Wild Shape and convert them into a single spell slot, with each use contributing 2 spell levels. For example, if you convert two uses of Wild Shape, you produce a level 4 spell slot. Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Longevity
entries: The primal magic that you wield causes you to age more slowly. For every ten years that pass, your body ages only one year.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You have honed your martial prowess and gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice. {@feat Defense|SRD52} is recommended.
Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS}.

classFeature.name: Second Wind
entries: You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can use it to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} equal to {@dice 1d10} plus your Fighter level.
You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter Features table.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of three kinds of {@filter Simple|items|type=simple weapon} or {@filter Martial|items|type=martial weapon} weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Fighter levels, you gain the ability to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Fighter Features table.

classFeature.name: Action Surge
entries: You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the {@action Magic|SRD52} action.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

classFeature.name: Tactical Mind
entries: You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success. Rather than regaining {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52}, you roll {@dice 1d10} and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.

classFeature.name: Fighter Subclass
entries: You gain a Fighter subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Fighter levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Fighter level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 6, 8, 12, 14, and 16.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Tactical Shift
entries: Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|SRD52} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|SRD52|Opportunity Attacks}.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Fighter Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Indomitable
entries: If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
You can use this feature twice before a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} starting at level 13 and three times before a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} starting at level 17.

classFeature.name: Tactical Master
entries: When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the {@itemMastery Push|SRD52}, {@itemMastery Sap|SRD52}, or {@itemMastery Slow|SRD52} property for that attack.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Fighter Subclass.

classFeature.name: Two Extra Attacks
entries: You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Indomitable
entries: If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
You can use this feature twice before a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} starting at level 13 and three times before a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} starting at level 17.

classFeature.name: Studied Attacks
entries: You study your opponents and learn from each attack you make. If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Fighter Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Action Surge
entries: You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the {@action Magic|SRD52} action.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. Starting at level 17, you can use it twice before a rest but only once on a turn.

classFeature.name: Indomitable
entries: If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
You can use this feature twice before a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} starting at level 13 and three times before a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} starting at level 17.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Fighter Subclass.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Combat Prowess|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Three Extra Attacks
entries: You can attack four times instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Bonus Unarmed Strike
entries: You can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Dexterous Attacks
entries: You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Unarmed Strikes and Monk weapons. In addition, when you use the Grapple or Shove option of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52}, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to determine the save DC.

classFeature.name: Martial Arts
entries: Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52} and Monk weapons, which are the following:

items: {@filter Martial Melee Weapons that have the Light property|items|type=martial weapon;melee weapon=sand|property=light}

entries: You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only Monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Martial Arts Die
entries: You can roll {@damage 1d6} in place of the normal damage of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52} or Monk weapons. This die changes as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk Features table.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|SRD52}, your base {@variantrule Armor Class|SRD52} equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.

classFeature.name: Flurry of Blows
entries: You can expend 1 Focus Point to make two Unarmed Strikes as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Monk's Focus
entries: Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy within yourself. This energy is represented by Focus Points. Your Monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Focus Points column of the Monk Features table.
You can expend these points to enhance or fuel certain Monk features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind, each of which is detailed below.
When you expend a Focus Point, it is unavailable until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, at the end of which you regain all your expended points.
Some features that use Focus Points require your target to make a saving throw. The save DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus}.

classFeature.name: Patient Defense
entries: You can take the {@action Disengage|SRD52} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}. Alternatively, you can expend 1 Focus Point to take both the {@action Disengage|SRD52} and the {@action Dodge|SRD52} actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Step of the Wind
entries: You can take the {@action Dash|SRD52} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}. Alternatively, you can expend 1 Focus Point to take both the {@action Disengage|SRD52} and {@action Dash|SRD52} actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Movement
entries: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|SRD52}. This bonus increases when you reach certain Monk levels, as shown on the Monk Features table.

classFeature.name: Uncanny Metabolism
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52}, you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your Martial Arts die, and regain a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Deflect Attacks
entries: When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|SRD52} to reduce the attack's total damage against you. The reduction equals {@dice 1d10} plus your Dexterity modifier and Monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect some of the attack's force. If you do so, choose a creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself if the attack was a melee attack or a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that isn't behind {@variantrule Cover|SRD52|Total Cover} if the attack was a ranged attack. That creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die plus your Dexterity modifier. The damage is the same type dealt by the attack.

classFeature.name: Monk Subclass
entries: You gain a Monk subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Monk levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Monk level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Monk levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Slow Fall
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Reaction|SRD52} when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Stunning Strike
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52}, you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Stunned|SRD52} condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target's {@variantrule Speed|SRD52} is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against the target before then has {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Empowered Strikes
entries: Whenever you deal damage with your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52}, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

classFeature.name: Evasion
entries: When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.
You don't benefit from this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Acrobatic Movement
entries: While you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|SRD52}, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.

classFeature.name: Heightened Focus
entries: Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Flurry of Blows
entries: You can expend 1 Focus Point to use Flurry of Blows and make three Unarmed Strikes with it instead of two.

entries.name: Patient Defense
entries: When you expend a Focus Point to use Patient Defense, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|SRD52} equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.

entries.name: Step of the Wind
entries: When you expend a Focus Point to use Step of the Wind, you can choose a willing creature within 5 feet of yourself that is Large or smaller. You move the creature with you until the end of your turn. The creature's movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|SRD52|Opportunity Attacks}.

classFeature.name: Self-Restoration
entries: Through sheer force of will, you can remove one of the following conditions from yourself at the end of each of your turns: {@condition Charmed|SRD52}, {@condition Frightened|SRD52}, or {@condition Poisoned|SRD52}.
In addition, forgoing food and drink doesn't give you levels of {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Deflect Energy
entries: You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

classFeature.name: Disciplined Survivor
entries: Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws.
Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.

classFeature.name: Perfect Focus
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52} and don't use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Monk subclass.

classFeature.name: Superior Defense
entries: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition. During that time, you have {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} to all damage except Force damage.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Irresistible Offense|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Body and Mind
entries: You have developed your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

classFeature.name: Lay on Hands
entries: Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. With that pool, you can restore a total number of {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} equal to five times your Paladin level.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can touch a creature (which could be yourself) and draw power from the pool of healing to restore a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool.

You can also expend 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} from the pool of healing power to remove the {@condition Poisoned|SRD52} condition from the creature; those points don't also restore {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} to the creature.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See {@book chapter 7|SRD52|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Paladin spells, which appear in the {@filter Paladin spell list|spells|class=Paladin} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Paladin Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two {@filter level 1 Paladin spells|spells|class=Paladin|level=1}. {@spell Heroism|SRD52} and {@spell Searing Smite|SRD52} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Paladin levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Paladin Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Paladin spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Paladin Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Paladin, your list of prepared spells can include six Paladin spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Paladin feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Paladin spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can replace one spell on your list with another Paladin spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Paladin spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use a {@item Holy Symbol|SRD52} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|SRD52} for your Paladin spells.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of two kinds of {@filter weapons|items|type=simple weapon;martial weapon} of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Longsword|SRD52|Longswords} and {@item Javelin|SRD52|Javelins}.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of {@item Halberd|SRD52|Halberds} and {@item Flail|SRD52|Flails}.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

classFeature.name: Paladin's Smite
entries: You always have the {@spell Divine Smite|SRD52} spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} before you can cast it in this way again.

classFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes, using it to fuel magical effects. You start with one such effect: Divine Sense, which is described below. Other Paladin features give additional Channel Divinity effect options. Each time you use this class's Channel Divinity, you choose which effect from this class to create.

You can use this class's Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. You gain an additional use when you reach Paladin level 11.
If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class's Spellcasting feature.

classFeature.name: Divine Sense
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can open your awareness to detect Celestials, Fiends, and Undead. For the next 10 minutes or until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition, you know the location of any creature of those types within 60 feet of yourself, and you know its creature type. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the {@spell Hallow|SRD52} spell.

classFeature.name: Paladin Subclass
entries: You gain a Paladin subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Paladin levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Paladin level or lower.

entries.name: Breaking Your Oath
entries: A Paladin tries to hold to the highest standards of conduct, but even the most dedicated are fallible. Sometimes a Paladin transgresses their oath.
A Paladin who has broken a vow typically seeks absolution, spending an all-night vigil as a sign of penitence or undertaking a fast. After a rite of forgiveness, the Paladin starts fresh.
If your Paladin unrepentantly violates their oath, talk to your DM. Your Paladin should probably take a more appropriate subclass or even abandon the class and adopt another one.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Paladin levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Faithful Steed
entries: You can call on the aid of an otherworldly steed. You always have the {@spell Find Steed|SRD52} spell prepared.
You can also cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Aura of Protection
entries: You radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|SRD52|Emanation} that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition.
You and your allies in the aura gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum bonus of +1).
If another Paladin is present, a creature can benefit from only one Aura of Protection at a time; the creature chooses which aura while in them.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Paladin Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Abjure Foes
entries: As a {@action Magic|SRD52} action, you can expend one use of this class's Channel Divinity to overwhelm foes with awe. As you present your {@item Holy Symbol|SRD52} or weapon, you can target a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|SRD52} condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. While {@condition Frightened|SRD52} in this way, a target can do only one of the following on its turns: move, take an action, or take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Aura of Courage
entries: You and your allies have {@variantrule Immunity|SRD52} to the {@condition Frightened|SRD52} condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a {@condition Frightened|SRD52} ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

classFeature.name: Radiant Strikes
entries: Your strikes now carry supernatural power. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52}, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Radiant damage.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Restoring Touch
entries: When you use Lay On Hands on a creature, you can also remove one or more of the following conditions from the creature: {@condition Blinded|SRD52}, {@condition Charmed|SRD52}, {@condition Deafened|SRD52}, {@condition Frightened|SRD52}, {@condition Paralyzed|SRD52}, or {@condition Stunned|SRD52}. You must expend 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} from the healing pool of Lay On Hands for each of these conditions you remove; those points don't also restore {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52} to the creature.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Paladin Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Aura Expansion
entries: Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|SRD52|Emanation}.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Truesight|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Paladin Subclass.

classFeature.name: Favored Enemy
entries: You always have the {@spell Hunter's Mark|SRD52} spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
The number of times you can cast the spell without a spell slot increases when you reach certain Ranger levels, as shown in the Favored Enemy column of the Ranger Features table.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See {@book chapter 7|SRD52|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Ranger spells, which appear in the {@filter Ranger spell list|spells|class=Ranger} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Ranger Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
