entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two {@filter level 1 Ranger spells|spells|class=Ranger|level=1}. {@spell Cure Wounds|SRD52} and {@spell Ensnaring Strike|SRD52} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Ranger levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Ranger Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Ranger spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Ranger Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Ranger, your list of prepared spells can include six Ranger spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Ranger feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Ranger spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can replace one spell on your list with another Ranger spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Ranger spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use a {@item Druidic Focus|SRD52} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|SRD52} for your Ranger spells.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of two kinds of {@filter weapons|items|type=simple weapon;martial weapon} of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Longbow|SRD52|Longbows} and {@item Shortsword|SRD52|Shortswords}.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of {@item Scimitar|SRD52|Scimitars} and {@item Longsword|SRD52|Longswords}.

classFeature.name: Deft Explorer
entries: Thanks to your travels, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Expertise
entries: Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52}. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in that skill.

entries.name: Languages
entries: You know two languages of your choice from the language tables in {@book chapter 2|SRD52|2|Choose Languages}.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a {@filter Fighting Style feat|feats|category=FS} of your choice. Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

classFeature.name: Ranger Subclass
entries: You gain a Ranger subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Ranger levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Ranger level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Ranger levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Roving
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|SRD52} increases by 10 feet while you aren't wearing Heavy armor. You also have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|SRD52} and a {@variantrule Swim Speed|SRD52} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Ranger Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52}. You gain {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in those skills.

classFeature.name: Tireless
entries: Primal forces now help fuel you on your journeys, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: As a {@action Magic|SRD52} action, you can give yourself a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|SRD52} equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). You can use this action a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Decrease Exhaustion
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, your {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52} level, if any, decreases by 1.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Ranger Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Relentless Hunter
entries: Taking damage can't break your {@status Concentration|SRD52} on Hunter's Mark.

classFeature.name: Nature's Veil
entries: You invoke spirits of nature to magically hide yourself. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can give yourself the {@condition Invisible|SRD52} condition until the end of your next turn.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Ranger Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Precise Hunter
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter's Mark.

classFeature.name: Feral Senses
entries: Your connection to the forces of nature grants you {@sense Blindsight|SRD52} with a range of 30 feet.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Dimensional Travel|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Foe Slayer
entries: The damage die of your Hunter's Mark is a {@damage d10} rather than a {@damage d6}.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. {@skill Sleight of Hand|SRD52} and {@skill Stealth|SRD52} are recommended if you have proficiency in them.
At Rogue level 6, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

classFeature.name: Sneak Attack
entries: You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

You don't need {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition, and you don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|SRD52} on the attack roll.
The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.

classFeature.name: Thieves' Cant
entries: You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in {@book chapter 2|SRD52|2|Choose Languages}.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of two kinds of {@filter weapons|items|type=simple weapon;martial weapon} of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Dagger|SRD52|Daggers} and {@item Shortbow|SRD52|Shortbows}.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the {@variantrule weapon mastery properties|SRD52|mastery properties} of {@item Scimitar|SRD52|Scimitars} and {@item Shortsword|SRD52|Shortswords}.

classFeature.name: Cunning Action
entries: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}: {@action Dash|SRD52}, {@action Disengage|SRD52}, or {@action Hide|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Rogue Subclass
entries: You gain a Rogue subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Rogue levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Rogue level or lower.

classFeature.name: Steady Aim
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your {@variantrule Speed|SRD52} is 0 until the end of the current turn.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Rogue levels 8, 10, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Cunning Strike
entries: You've developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling, and the effect occurs immediately after the attack's damage is dealt. For example, if you add the Poison effect, remove {@dice 1d6} from the Sneak Attack's damage before rolling.
If a Cunning Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus}.

classFeature.name: Poison (Cost: 1d6)
entries: You add a toxin to your strike, forcing the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Poisoned|SRD52} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the {@condition Poisoned|SRD52} target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
To use this effect, you must have a {@item Poisoner's Kit|SRD52} on your person.

classFeature.name: Trip (Cost: 1d6)
entries: If the target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|SRD52} condition.

classFeature.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|SRD52} to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

classFeature.name: Withdraw (Cost: 1d6)
entries: Immediately after the attack, you move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|SRD52} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|SRD52|Opportunity Attacks}.

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in two of your Skill Proficiencies of your choice.

classFeature.name: Evasion
entries: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition.

classFeature.name: Reliable Talent
entries: Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Improved Cunning Strike
entries: You can use up to two Cunning Strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Daze (Cost: 2d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or on its next turn, it can do only one of the following: move or take an action or a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Devious Strikes
entries: You've practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack deviously. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

classFeature.name: Knock Out (Cost: 6d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or it has the {@condition Unconscious|SRD52} condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. The {@condition Unconscious|SRD52} target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

classFeature.name: Obscure (Cost: 3d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, or it has the {@condition Blinded|SRD52} condition until the end of its next turn.

classFeature.name: Slippery Mind
entries: Your cunning mind is exceptionally difficult to control. You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Elusive
entries: You're so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll can have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} against you unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of the Night Spirit|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Stroke of Luck
entries: You have a marvelous knack for succeeding when you need to. If you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|SRD52}, you can turn the roll into a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Innate Sorcery
entries: An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can unleash that magic for 1 minute, during which you gain the following benefits:

items: The spell save DC of your Sorcerer spells increases by 1.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on the attack rolls of Sorcerer spells you cast.

entries: You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: Drawing from your innate magic, you can cast spells. See {@book chapter 7|SRD52|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Sorcerer spells, which appear in the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know four Sorcerer cantrips of your choice. {@spell Light|SRD52}, {@spell Prestidigitation|SRD52}, {@spell Shocking Grasp|SRD52}, and {@spell Sorcerous Burst|SRD52} are recommended. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Sorcerer levels 4 and 10, you learn another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Sorcerer Features table.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Sorcerer spells. {@spell Burning Hands|SRD52} and {@spell Detect Magic|SRD52} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Sorcerer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Sorcerer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Sorcerer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Sorcerer Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Sorcerer, your list of prepared spells can include six Sorcerer spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Sorcerer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Sorcerer spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|SRD52} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|SRD52} for your Sorcerer spells.

classFeature.name: Font of Magic
entries: You can tap into the wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by Sorcery Points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.

You have 2 Sorcery Points, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Sorcery Points column of the Sorcerer Features table. You can't have more Sorcery Points than the number shown in the table for your level. You regain all expended Sorcery Points when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
You can use your Sorcery Points to fuel the options below, along with other features, such as Metamagic, that use those points.

entries.name: Converting Spell Slots to Sorcery Points
entries: You can expend a spell slot to gain a number of Sorcery Points equal to the slot's level (no action required).

entries.name: Creating Spell Slots
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can transform unexpended Sorcery Points into one spell slot. The Creating Spell Slots table shows the cost of creating a spell slot of a given level, and it lists the minimum Sorcerer level you must be to create a slot. You can create a spell slot no higher than level 5.
Any spell slot you create with this feature vanishes when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Metamagic
entries: Because your magic flows from within, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from "{@filter Metamagic Options|optionalfeatures|feature type=MM|source=SRD52}" later in this class's description. You use the chosen options to temporarily modify spells you cast. To use an option, you must spend the number of Sorcery Points that it costs.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it unless otherwise noted in one of those options.
Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don't know. You gain two more options at Sorcerer level 10 and two more at Sorcerer level 17.

classFeature.name: Metamagic Options
entries: The following options are available to your Metamagic feature. The options are presented in alphabetical order.

classFeature.name: Sorcerer Subclass
entries: You gain a Sorcerer subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Sorcerer levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Sorcerer level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Sorcerer levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Sorcerous Restoration
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, you can regain expended Sorcery Points, but no more than a number equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Sorcerer subclass.

classFeature.name: Sorcery Incarnate
entries: If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can use it if you spend 2 Sorcery Points when you take the {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52} to activate it.
In addition, while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use up to two of your {@filter Metamagic options|optionalfeatures|feature type=MM} on each spell you cast.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Metamagic
entries: Because your magic flows from within you, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from the "{@filter Metamagic Options|optionalfeatures|feature type=MM|source=SRD52}" section later in this class's description.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted in one of those options.
Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don't know.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Sorcerer subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Metamagic
entries: Because your magic flows from within you, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from the "{@filter Metamagic Options|optionalfeatures|feature type=MM|source=SRD52}" section later in this class's description.
You can use only one Metamagic option on a spell when you cast it, unless otherwise noted in one of those options.
Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your Metamagic options with one you don't know.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Sorcerer subclass.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Dimensional Travel|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Arcane Apotheosis
entries: While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on it.

classFeature.name: Eldritch Invocation Options
entries: Eldritch Invocation options appear in alphabetical order.

classFeature.name: Eldritch Invocations
entries: You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome. Invocations are described in the "{@filter Eldritch Invocation Options|optionalfeatures|feature type=EI|source=SRD52}" section later in this class's description.

entries.name: Prerequisites
entries: If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Warlock level 5.

entries.name: Replacing and Gaining Invocations
entries: Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.
When you gain certain Warlock levels, you gain more invocations of your choice, as shown in the Invocations column of the Warlock Features table.
You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

classFeature.name: Pact Magic
entries: Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers. The entity is a voice in the shadows—its identity unclear—but its boon to you is concrete: the ability to cast spells. See {@book chapter 7|SRD52|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Warlock spells, which appear in the {@filter Warlock spell list|spells|class=Warlock} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know two Warlock cantrips of your choice. {@spell Eldritch Blast|SRD52} and {@spell Prestidigitation|SRD52} are recommended. Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Warlock cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Warlock levels 4 and 10, you learn another Warlock cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Warlock Features table.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

For example, when you're a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell {@spell Witch Bolt|SRD52}, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. {@spell Charm Person|SRD52} and {@spell Hex|SRD52} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Warlock levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warlock Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Warlock spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 6, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1–3.

If another Warlock feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Warlock spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Warlock spell of an eligible level.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Charisma is the spellcasting ability for your Warlock spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|SRD52} as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|SRD52} for your Warlock spells.

classFeature.name: Magical Cunning
entries: You can perform an esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots but no more than a number equal to half your maximum (round up). Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Warlock Subclass
entries: You gain a Warlock subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Warlock levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Warlock level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Warlock levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Warlock subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Contact Patron
entries: In the past, you usually contacted your patron through intermediaries. Now you can communicate directly; you always have the {@spell Contact Other Plane|SRD52} spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot to contact your patron, and you automatically succeed on the spell's saving throw.
Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Warlock subclass.

classFeature.name: Mystic Arcanum
entries: Your patron grants you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum.
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} before you can cast it in this way again.

As shown in the Warlock Features table, you gain another Warlock spell of your choice that can be cast in this way when you reach Warlock levels 13 (level 7 spell), 15 (level 8 spell), and 17 (level 9 spell). You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your arcanum spells with another Warlock spell of the same level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Mystic Arcanum
entries: You gain a level 7 Warlock Spell of your choice.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Warlock subclass.

classFeature.name: Mystic Arcanum
entries: You gain a level 8 Warlock Spell of your choice.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Mystic Arcanum
entries: You gain a level 9 Warlock Spell of your choice.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Fate|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Eldritch Master
entries: When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots.

classFeature.name: Arcane Recovery
entries: You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

classFeature.name: Ritual Adept
entries: You can cast any spell as a {@variantrule Ritual|SRD52} if that spell has the {@variantrule Ritual|SRD52} tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See {@book chapter 7|SRD52|7} for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the {@filter Wizard spell list|spells|class=Wizard} later in the class's description.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. {@spell Light|SRD52}, {@spell Mage Hand|SRD52}, and {@spell Ray of Frost|SRD52} are recommended. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.

entries.name: Spellbook
entries: Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds, contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting {@spell Identify|SRD52}. You determine the book's appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.

The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice. {@spell Detect Magic|SRD52}, {@spell Feather Fall|SRD52}, {@spell Mage Armor|SRD52}, {@spell Magic Missile|SRD52}, {@spell Sleep|SRD52}, and {@spell Thunderwave|SRD52} are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table. The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of Level 1+
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.

If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus|SRD52} or your spellbook as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|SRD52} for your Wizard spells.

entries.name: Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook
entries: The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect your ongoing magical research, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to the book. You could discover a Wizard spell on a {@item Spell Scroll|SRD52}, for example, and then copy it into your spellbook.

entries.name: Copying a Spell into the Book
entries: When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it's of a level you can prepare and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Afterward you can prepare the spell like the other spells in your spellbook.

entries.name: Copying the Book
entries: You can copy a spell from your spellbook into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your spellbook but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the Wizard spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep a backup spellbook.

classFeature.name: Scholar
entries: While studying magic, you also specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: {@skill Arcana|SRD52}, {@skill History|SRD52}, {@skill Investigation|SRD52}, {@skill Medicine|SRD52}, {@skill Nature|SRD52}, or {@skill Religion|SRD52}. You have {@variantrule Expertise|SRD52} in the chosen skill.

classFeature.name: Wizard Subclass
entries: You gain a Wizard subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Wizard levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Wizard level or lower.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Memorize Spell
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52}, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Wizard Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Wizard Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Wizard Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement|SRD52} Feat or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Spell Mastery
entries: You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you can study your spellbook and replace one of those spells with an eligible spell of the same level from the book.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@filter Epic Boon feat|feats|category=EB} or another {@5etools feat|feats.html} of your choice for which you qualify. {@feat Boon of Spell Recall|SRD52} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Signature Spells
entries: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't cast them in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

condition.name: Blinded
entries: While you have the Blinded condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Can't See
entries: You can't see and automatically fail any ability check that requires sight.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: {@action Attack|srd52} rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52}, and your attack rolls have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52}.

condition.name: Charmed
entries: While you have the Charmed condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Can't Harm the Charmer
entries: You can't attack the charmer or target the charmer with damaging abilities or {@variantrule Magical Effect|srd52|magical effects}.

entries.name: Social Advantage
entries: The charmer has {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} on any ability check to interact with you socially.

condition.name: Deafened
entries: While you have the Deafened condition, you experience the following effect.

entries.name: Can't Hear
entries: You can't hear and automatically fail any ability check that requires hearing.

condition.name: Exhaustion
entries: While you have the Exhaustion condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Exhaustion Levels
entries: This condition is cumulative. Each time you receive it, you gain 1 Exhaustion level. You die if your Exhaustion level is 6.

entries.name: D20 Tests Affected
entries: When you make a D20 Test, the roll is reduced by 2 times your Exhaustion level.

entries.name: Speed Reduced
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} is reduced by a number of feet equal to 5 times your Exhaustion level.

entries.name: Removing Exhaustion Levels
entries: Finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|srd52} removes 1 of your Exhaustion levels. When your Exhaustion level reaches 0, the condition ends.

condition.name: Frightened
entries: While you have the Frightened condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Ability Checks and Attacks Affected
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight.

entries.name: Can't Approach
entries: You can't willingly move closer to the source of fear.

condition.name: Grappled
entries: While you have the Grappled condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Speed 0
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} is 0 and can't increase.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on attack rolls against any target other than the grappler.

entries.name: Movable
entries: The grappler can drag or carry you when it moves, but every foot of movement costs it 1 extra foot unless you are Tiny or two or more sizes smaller than it.

condition.name: Incapacitated
entries: While you have the Incapacitated condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Inactive
entries: You can't take any {@variantrule Action|srd52|action}, {@variantrule Bonus Action|srd52}, or {@variantrule Reaction|srd52}.

entries.name: No Concentration
entries: Your {@status Concentration|srd52} is broken.

entries.name: Speechless
entries: You can't speak.

entries.name: Surprised
entries: If you're Incapacitated when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|srd52}, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on the roll.

condition.name: Invisible
entries: While you have the Invisible condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Surprise
entries: If you're Invisible when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|srd52}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} on the roll.

entries.name: Concealed
entries: You aren't affected by any effect that requires its target to be seen unless the effect's creator can somehow see you. Any equipment you are wearing or carrying is also concealed.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: {@action Attack|srd52} rolls against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52}, and your attack rolls have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52}. If a creature can somehow see you, you don't gain this benefit against that creature.

condition.name: Paralyzed
entries: While you have the Paralyzed condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Incapacitated
entries: You have the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} condition.

entries.name: Speed 0
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} is 0 and can't increase.

entries.name: Saving Throws Affected
entries: You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throws}.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: {@action Attack|srd52} rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52}.

entries.name: Automatic Critical Hits
entries: Any attack roll that hits you is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|srd52} if the attacker is within 5 feet of you.

condition.name: Petrified
entries: While you have the Petrified condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Turned to Inanimate Substance
entries: You are transformed, along with any nonmagical objects you are wearing and carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone). Your weight increases by a factor of ten, and you cease aging.

entries.name: Incapacitated
entries: You have the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} condition.

entries.name: Speed 0
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} is 0 and can't increase.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: {@action Attack|srd52} rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52}.

entries.name: Saving Throws Affected
entries: You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throws}.

entries.name: Resist Damage
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|srd52} to all damage.

entries.name: Poison Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|srd52} to the {@condition Poisoned|srd52} condition.

condition.name: Poisoned
entries: While you have the Poisoned condition, you experience the following effect.

entries.name: Ability Checks and Attacks Affected
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on attack rolls and ability checks.

condition.name: Prone
entries: While you have the Prone condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Restricted Movement
entries: Your only movement options are to {@variantrule Crawling|srd52|crawl} or to spend an amount of movement equal to half your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} (round down) to right yourself and thereby end the condition. If your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} is 0, you can't right yourself.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on attack rolls. An attack roll against you has {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} if the attacker is within 5 feet of you. Otherwise, that attack roll has {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52}.

condition.name: Restrained
entries: While you have the Restrained condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Speed 0
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} is 0 and can't increase.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: {@action Attack|srd52} rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52}, and your attack rolls have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52}.

entries.name: Saving Throws Affected
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throws}.

condition.name: Stunned
entries: While you have the Stunned condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Incapacitated
entries: You have the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} condition.

entries.name: Saving Throws Affected
entries: You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throws}.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: {@action Attack|srd52} rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52}.

condition.name: Unconscious
entries: While you have the Unconscious condition, you experience the following effects.

entries.name: Inert
entries: You have the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} and {@condition Prone|srd52} conditions, and you drop whatever you're holding. When this condition ends, you remain {@condition Prone|srd52}.

entries.name: Speed 0
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|srd52} is 0 and can't increase.

entries.name: Attacks Affected
entries: {@action Attack|srd52} rolls against you have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52}.

entries.name: Saving Throws Affected
entries: You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throws}.

entries.name: Automatic Critical Hits
entries: Any attack roll that hits you is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|srd52} if the attacker is within 5 feet of you.

entries.name: Unaware
entries: You're unaware of your surroundings.

disease.name: Cackle Fever
entries: Cheaply made potions and elixirs are sometimes tainted by Cackle Fever, which affects Humanoids only (gnomes are strangely immune). A creature suffers the following effects {@dice 1d4} days after infection:

items.name: Fever
items.entry: The creature gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52} level, which lasts until the contagion ends on the creature.

items.name: Uncontrollable Laughter
items.entry: While the creature has the {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52} condition, the creature makes a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw each time it takes damage other than Psychic damage. On a failed save, the creature takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Psychic damage and has the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition as it laughs uncontrollably. At the end of each of its turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically.

entries.name: Fighting the Contagion
entries: At the end of each Long Rest, an infected creature makes a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw. After the creature succeeds on three of these saves, the contagion ends on it, and the creature is immune to Cackle Fever for 1 year.

entries.name: Spreading the Contagion
entries: Any Humanoid (other than a gnome) that starts its turn within a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|SRD52|Emanation} originating from a creature infected with Cackle Fever must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or also become infected with the contagion. On a successful save, the Humanoid can't catch the contagion from that particular infected creature for the next 24 hours.

disease.name: Sewer Plague
entries: Fouled potions and alchemical waste can give rise to Sewer Plague, which incubates in sewers and refuse heaps and is sometimes transmitted by creatures that dwell in such areas, including otyughs and rats. Any Humanoid that is wounded by a creature that carries the contagion or that comes into contact with contaminated filth or offal must succeed on a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw or become infected with Sewer Plague. A creature suffers the following effects {@dice 1d4} days after infection:

items.name: Weakness
items.entry: While the creature has any Exhaustion levels, it regains only half the normal number of Hit Points from spending Hit Point Dice.

items.name: Restlessness
items.entry: While the creature has any Exhaustion levels, finishing a Long Rest neither restores lost Hit Points nor reduces the creature's Exhaustion level.

entries.name: Fighting the Contagion
entries: Daily at dawn, an infected creature makes a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52} level as its fatigue worsens. On a successful save, the creature's Exhaustion level decreases by 1. If the creature's Exhaustion level is reduced to 0, the contagion ends on the creature.

disease.name: Sight Rot
entries: Any Beast or Humanoid that drinks water tainted by Sight Rot must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Blinded|SRD52} condition until the contagion ends.

entries.name: Fighting the Contagion
entries: Magic such as a {@spell Heal|SRD52} or {@spell Lesser Restoration|SRD52} spell ends the contagion immediately. A character who is proficient with an {@item Herbalism Kit|SRD52} can use it to create one dose of nonmagical ointment, which takes 1 hour. When applied to the eyes of a creature suffering from Sight Rot, the ointment suppresses the contagion on that creature for 24 hours. If the contagion is suppressed in this way for a total of 72 hours (requiring three doses and applications of the ointment), the contagion ends on the creature.

entries.name: Spreading the Contagion
entries: Any Humanoid that makes skin contact with a creature infected with Sight Rot must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or also become infected with the contagion. On a successful save, the Humanoid can't catch the contagion from that particular infected creature for the next 24 hours.

feat.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: Increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. This feat can't increase an ability score above 20.

entries.name: Repeatable
entries: You can take this feat more than once.

feat.name: Alert
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Initiative Proficiency
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52}, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus} to the roll.

entries.name: Initiative Swap
entries: Immediately after you roll {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52}, you can swap your {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52} with the {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52} of one willing ally in the same combat. You can't make this swap if you or the ally has the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition.

feat.name: Archery
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with Ranged weapons.

feat.name: Boon of Combat Prowess
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Peerless Aim
entries: When you miss with an attack roll, you can hit instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.

feat.name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Blink Steps
entries: Immediately after you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action or the {@action Magic|SRD52} action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

feat.name: Boon of Fate
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Improve Fate
entries: When you or another creature within 60 feet of you succeeds on or fails a {@variantrule D20 Test|SRD52}, you can roll {@dice 2d4} and apply the total rolled as a bonus or penalty to the {@dice d20} roll. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you roll {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52} or finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

feat.name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Overcome Defenses
entries: The Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you deal always ignores {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52}.

entries.name: Overwhelming Strike
entries: When you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll, you can deal extra damage to the target equal to the ability score increased by this feat. The extra damage's type is the same as the attack's type.

feat.name: Boon of Spell Recall
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Free Casting
entries: Whenever you cast a spell with a level 1-4 spell slot, roll {@dice 1d4}. If the number you roll is the same as the slot's level, the slot isn't expended.

feat.name: Boon of the Night Spirit
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Merge with Shadows
entries: While within {@variantrule Dim Light|SRD52} or {@variantrule Darkness|SRD52}, you can give yourself the {@condition Invisible|SRD52} condition as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}. The condition ends on you immediately after you take an action, a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, or a {@variantrule Reaction|SRD52}.

entries.name: Shadowy Form
entries: While within {@variantrule Dim Light|SRD52} or {@variantrule Darkness|SRD52}, you have {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} to all damage except Psychic and Radiant.

feat.name: Boon of Truesight
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Truesight
entries: You have {@sense Truesight|SRD52} with a range of 60 feet.

feat.name: Defense
entries: While you're wearing Light, Medium, or Heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|SRD52}.

feat.name: Grappler
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Punch and Grab
entries: When you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|SRD52} as part of the {@action Attack|SRD52} action on your turn, you can use both the Damage and the Grapple option. You can use this benefit only once per turn.

entries.name: Attack Advantage
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on attack rolls against a creature {@condition Grappled|SRD52} by you.

entries.name: Fast Wrestler
entries: You don't have to spend extra movement to move a creature {@condition Grappled|SRD52} by you if the creature is your size or smaller.

feat.name: Great Weapon Fighting
entries: When you roll damage for an attack you make with a Melee weapon that you are holding with two hands, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3. The weapon must have the {@itemProperty 2h|SRD52|Two-Handed} or {@itemProperty V|SRD52|Versatile} property to gain this benefit.

feat.name: Magic Initiate
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Two Cantrips
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Cleric|spells|level=0;1|class=Cleric}, {@filter Druid|spells|level=0;1|class=Druid}, or {@filter Wizard|spells|level=0;1|class=Wizard} spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

entries.name: Level 1 Spell
entries: Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat's cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

entries.name: Spell Change
entries: Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list.

entries.name: Repeatable
entries: You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.

items.name: Two Cantrips
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Cleric|spells|level=0;1|class=Cleric} spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

items.name: Level 1 Spell
entries: Choose a level 1 spell from the {@filter Cleric|spells|level=0;1|class=Cleric} spell list. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

items.name: Two Cantrips
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Druid|spells|level=0;1|class=Druid} spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

items.name: Level 1 Spell
entries: Choose a level 1 spell from the {@filter Druid|spells|level=0;1|class=Druid} spell list. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

items.name: Two Cantrips
entries: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Wizard|spells|level=0;1|class=Wizard} spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

items.name: Level 1 Spell
entries: Choose a level 1 spell from the {@filter Wizard|spells|level=0;1|class=Wizard} spell list. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

feat.name: Savage Attacker
entries: You've trained to deal particularly damaging strikes. Once per turn when you hit a target with a weapon, you can roll the weapon's damage dice twice and use either roll against the target.

feat.name: Skilled
entries: You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or {@filter tools|items|type=tool;artisan's tools;instrument;gaming set} of your choice.

entries.name: Repeatable
entries: You can take this feat more than once.

feat.name: Two-Weapon Fighting
entries: When you make an extra attack as a result of using a weapon that has the {@itemProperty L|SRD52|Light} property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren't already adding it to the damage.

hazard.name: Burning
entries: A burning creature or object takes {@damage 1d4} Fire damage at the start of each of its turns. As an action, you can extinguish fire on yourself by giving yourself the {@condition Prone|srd52} condition and rolling on the ground. The fire also goes out if it is doused, submerged, or suffocated.

hazard.name: Deep Water
entries: Swimming through deep water (more than 100 feet deep) presents additional challenges because of the water's pressure and cold temperature. After each hour of swimming in deep water, a creature that lacks a Swim Speed must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52} level.

hazard.name: Dehydration
entries: A creature requires an amount of water per day based on its size, as shown in the Water Needs per Day table. A creature that drinks less than half the required water for a day gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} level at the day's end. {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} caused by dehydration can't be removed until the creature drinks the full amount of water required for a day.

hazard.name: Extreme Cold
entries: When the temperature is 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower, a creature exposed to the extreme cold must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52} level. Creatures that have {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} or {@variantrule Immunity|SRD52} to Cold damage automatically succeed on the save.

hazard.name: Extreme Heat
entries: When the temperature is 100 degrees Fahrenheit or higher, a creature exposed to the extreme heat and without access to drinkable water must succeed on a Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52} level. The DC is 5 for the first hour and increases by 1 for each additional hour. Creatures wearing Medium or Heavy armor have {@variantrule Disadvantage|SRD52} on the save. Creatures that have {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} or {@variantrule Immunity|SRD52} to Fire damage automatically succeed on the save.

hazard.name: Falling
entries: A creature that falls takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage at the end of the fall for every 10 feet it fell, to a maximum of {@damage 20d6}. When the creature lands, it has the {@condition Prone|srd52} condition unless it avoids taking any damage from the fall.

A creature that falls into water or another liquid can use its {@variantrule Reaction|srd52} to make a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|srd52}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|srd52}) check to hit the surface head or feet first. On a successful check, any damage resulting from the fall is halved.

hazard.name: Frigid Water
entries: A creature can be immersed in frigid water for a number of minutes equal to its Constitution score before suffering any ill effects. Each additional minute spent in frigid water requires the creature to succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|SRD52} level. Creatures with {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} or {@variantrule Immunity|SRD52} to Cold damage automatically succeed on the save, as do creatures that are naturally adapted to living in ice-cold water.

hazard.name: Heavy Precipitation
entries: Everything within an area of heavy rain or heavy snowfall is {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|SRD52}, and creatures in the area have {@variantrule Disadvantage|SRD52} on all Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) checks. Heavy rain also extinguishes open flames.

hazard.name: High Altitude
entries: Traveling at altitudes of 10,000 feet or higher above sea level is taxing for most creatures because of the reduced amount of oxygen in the air. Each hour such a creature spends traveling at high altitude counts as 2 hours for the purpose of determining how long that creature can travel (see "{@book Travel Pace|SRD52|1|Travel Pace}" in {@book chapter 2|SRD52|1}).

Creatures can become acclimated to a high altitude by spending 30 days or more at this elevation. Creatures can't become acclimated to elevations above 20,000 feet unless they are native to such environments.

hazard.name: Malnutrition
entries: A creature needs an amount of food per day based on its size, as shown in the Food Needs per Day table. A creature that eats but consumes less than half the required food for a day must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} level at the day's end. A creature that eats nothing for 5 days automatically gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} level at the end of the fifth day as well as an additional level at the end of each subsequent day without food.
{@condition Exhaustion|srd52} caused by malnutrition can't be removed until the creature eats the full amount of food required for a day.

hazard.name: Slippery Ice
entries: Slippery ice is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|SRD52}. A creature that moves onto slippery ice for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|SRD52} condition.

hazard.name: Strong Wind
entries: Strong wind imposes {@variantrule Disadvantage|SRD52} on ranged attack rolls with weapons. It also extinguishes open flames and disperses fog. A flying creature in a strong wind must land at the end of its turn or fall.
A strong wind in a desert can create a sandstorm that imposes Disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) checks.

hazard.name: Suffocation
entries: A creature can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 plus its Constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds) before suffocation begins. When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} level at the end of each of its turns. When a creature can breathe again, it removes all levels of {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} it gained from suffocating.

hazard.name: Thin Ice
entries: Thin ice has a weight tolerance of {@dice 3d10 × 10} pounds per 10-foot-square area. Whenever the total weight on an area of thin ice exceeds its tolerance, the ice in that area breaks. All creatures on broken ice fall through. Below the ice is {@hazard frigid water|SRD52}.

item.name: +1 Wand of the War Mage
item.reqAttune: by a spellcaster
entries: While holding this wand, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls. In addition, you ignore {@variantrule Cover|SRD52|Half Cover} when making a spell attack roll.

item.name: +2 Wand of the War Mage
item.reqAttune: by a spellcaster
entries: While holding this wand, you gain a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls. In addition, you ignore {@variantrule Cover|SRD52|Half Cover} when making a spell attack roll.

item.name: +3 Wand of the War Mage
item.reqAttune: by a spellcaster
entries: While holding this wand, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls. In addition, you ignore {@variantrule Cover|SRD52|Half Cover} when making a spell attack roll.

item.name: Acid
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a vial of Acid. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus}) or take {@damage 2d6} Acid damage.

item.name: Alchemist's Fire
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|SRD52} action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Alchemist's Fire. Target one creature or object you can see within 20 feet of yourself. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Dexterity modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|SRD52|Proficiency Bonus}) or take {@damage 1d4} Fire damage and start {@hazard burning|SRD52}.

item.name: Amulet
entries: For an Amulet to be an effective Holy Symbol, it must be worn or held.

item.name: Amulet of Health
entries: Your Constitution score is 19 while you wear this amulet. It has no effect on you if your Constitution is already 19 or higher without it.

item.name: Amulet of Proof against Detection and Location
entries: While wearing this amulet, you can't be targeted by Divination spells or perceived through magical scrying sensors unless you allow it.

item.name: Amulet of the Planes
entries: While wearing this amulet, you can take a {@action Magic|SRD52} action to name a location that you are familiar with on another plane of existence. Then make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|SRD52}) check. On a successful check, you cast {@spell Plane Shift|SRD52}. On a failed check, you and each creature and object within 15 feet of you travel to a random destination determined by rolling {@dice 1d100} and consulting the following table.

rows: Random location on the plane you named

Random location on an Inner Plane determined by rolling {@dice 1d6}: on a {@b 1}, the Plane of Air; on a {@b 2}, the Plane of Earth; on a {@b 3}, the Plane of Fire; on a {@b 4}, the Plane of Water; on a {@b 5}, the Feywild; on a {@b 6}, the Shadowfell

Random location on an Outer Plane determined by rolling 1d8: on a {@b 1}, Arborea; on a {@b 2}, Arcadia; on a {@b 3}, the Beastlands; on a {@b 4}, Bytopia; on a {@b 5}, Elysium; on a {@b 6}, Mechanus; on a {@b 7}, Mount Celestia; on an {@b 8}, Ysgard

Random location on an Outer Plane determined by rolling {@dice 1d8}: on a {@b 1}, the Abyss; on a {@b 2}, Acheron; on a {@b 3}, Carceri; on a {@b 4}, Gehenna; on a {@b 5}, Hades; on a {@b 6}, Limbo; on a {@b 7}, the Nine Hells; on an {@b 8}, Pandemonium
Random location on the Astral Plane

item.name: Animated Shield
entries: While holding this Shield, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52} to cause it to animate. The Shield leaps into the air and hovers in your space to protect you as if you were wielding it, leaving your hands free. The Shield remains animate for 1 minute, until you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52} to end this effect, or until you die or have the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition, at which point the Shield falls to the ground or into your hand if you have one free.

item.name: Antitoxin
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can drink a vial of Antitoxin to gain {@variantrule Advantage|SRD52} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|SRD52} condition for 1 hour.

item.name: Apparatus of the Crab
entries: This item first appears to be a sealed iron barrel weighing 500 pounds. The barrel has a hidden catch, which can be found with a successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|SRD52}) check. Releasing the catch unlocks a hatch at one end of the barrel, allowing two Medium or smaller creatures to crawl inside. Ten levers are set in a row at the far end, each in a neutral position, able to move up or down. When certain levers are used, the apparatus transforms to resemble a giant lobster.

The Apparatus of Kwalish is a Large object with the following statistics: {@b AC} 20; {@b HP} 200; {@b Speed} 30 ft., Swim 30 ft. (or 0 ft. for both if the legs aren't extended); {@b Immunity} to Poison and Psychic damage.

To be used as a vehicle, the apparatus requires one pilot. While the apparatus's hatch is closed, the compartment is airtight and watertight. The compartment holds enough air for 10 hours of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.
The apparatus floats on water. It can also go underwater to a depth of 900 feet. Below that, the vehicle takes {@damage 2d6} Bludgeoning damage each minute from pressure.

A creature in the compartment can take a {@action Utilize|SRD52} action to move as many as two of the apparatus's levers up or down. After each use, a lever goes back to its neutral position. Each lever, from left to right, functions as shown in the Apparatus of Kwalish Levers table.

entries.caption: Apparatus of Kwalish Levers
rows: Legs extend, allowing the apparatus to walk and swim.
Legs retract, reducing the apparatus's {@variantrule Speed|SRD52} and {@variantrule Swim Speed|SRD52} to 0 and making it unable to benefit from bonuses to speed.
Side window shutters open (two per side).
Side window shutters close (two per side).
Two claws extend from the front side of the apparatus.
Each extended claw makes the following melee attack: {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@i Hit:} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Bludgeoning damage.
Each extended claw makes the following melee attack: {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@i Hit:} The target has the {@condition Grappled|SRD52} condition (escape {@dc 15}).
The apparatus walks or swims forward provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus walks or swims backward provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus turns 90 degrees counterclockwise provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus turns 90 degrees clockwise provided its legs are extended.
Eyelike fixtures emit {@variantrule Bright Light|SRD52} in a 30-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|SRD52} for an additional 30 feet.
The apparatus sinks up to 20 feet if it's in liquid.
The apparatus rises up to 20 feet if it's in liquid.
The rear hatch unseals and opens.
The rear hatch closes and seals.

item.name: Armor of Invulnerability
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage while you wear this armor.

entries.name: Metal Shell
entries: You can take a {@action Magic|SRD52} action to give yourself {@variantrule Immunity|SRD52} to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage for 10 minutes or until you are no longer wearing the armor. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Arrow-Catching Shield
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|SRD52} against ranged attack rolls while you wield this Shield. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC.
Whenever an attacker makes a ranged attack roll against a target within 5 feet of you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|SRD52} to become the target of the attack instead.

item.name: Assassin's Blood
entries: A creature subjected to Assassin's Blood makes a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 6 ({@damage 1d12}) Poison damage and has the {@condition Poisoned|SRD52} condition for 24 hours. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only.

item.name: Backpack
entries: A Backpack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot. It can also serve as a saddlebag.

item.name: Bag of Beans
entries: This heavy cloth bag contains {@dice 3d4} dry beans when found. The bag weighs half a pound regardless of how many beans it contains and becomes a nonmagical item when it no longer contains any beans.

If you dump one or more beans out of the bag, they explode in a 10-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|SRD52|Sphere} centered on them. All the dumped beans are destroyed in the explosion, and each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|SRD52|Sphere}, including you, makes a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 5d4} Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

If you remove a bean from the bag, plant it in dirt or sand, and then water it, the bean disappears as it produces an effect 1 minute later from the ground where it was planted. The DM can choose an effect from the following table or determine it randomly.

rows: {@dice 5d4} toadstools sprout. If a creature eats a toadstool, roll any die. On an odd roll, the eater must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 5d6} Poison damage and have the {@condition Poisoned|SRD52} condition for 1 hour. On an even roll, the eater gains {@dice 5d6} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|SRD52} for 1 hour.
A geyser erupts and spouts water, beer, mayonnaise, tea, vinegar, wine, or oil (DM's choice) 30 feet into the air for {@dice 1d4} minutes.
A {@creature Treant|SRD52} sprouts. Roll any die. On an odd roll, the treant is Chaotic Evil. On an even roll, the treant is Chaotic Good.

An animate but immobile stone statue in your likeness rises and makes verbal threats against you. If you leave it and others come near, it describes you as the most heinous of villains and directs the newcomers to find and attack you. If you are on the same plane of existence as the statue, it knows where you are. The statue becomes inanimate after 24 hours.
A campfire with green flames springs forth and burns for 24 hours or until it is extinguished.

{@dice 1d4 + 4} bright-pink toads crawl forth. Whenever a toad is touched, it transforms into a Large or smaller monster of the DM's choice that acts in accordance with its alignment and nature. The monster remains for 1 minute, then disappears in a puff of bright-pink smoke.
A hungry {@creature Bulette|SRD52} burrows up and attacks.
A fruit tree grows. It has {@dice 1d10 + 20} fruit, {@dice 1d8} of which act as randomly determined potions. The tree vanishes after 1 hour. Picked fruit remains, retaining any magic for 30 days.

A nest of {@dice 1d4 + 3} rainbow-colored eggs springs up. Any creature that eats an egg makes a {@dc 20} Constitution saving throw. On a successful save, a creature permanently increases its lowest ability score by 1, randomly choosing among equally low scores. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 10d6} Force damage from an internal explosion.

A pyramid with a 60-foot-square base bursts upward. Inside is a burial chamber containing a {@creature Mummy|SRD52}, a {@creature Mummy Lord|SRD52}, or some other Undead of the DM's choice. Its sarcophagus contains treasure of the DM's choice.
A giant beanstalk sprouts, growing to a height of the DM's choice. The top leads where the DM chooses, such as to a great view, a cloud giant's castle, or another plane of existence.

item.name: Bag of Devouring
entries: This bag resembles a {@item Bag of Holding|SRD52} but is a feeding orifice for a gigantic extradimensional creature. Turning the bag inside out closes the orifice.

The extradimensional creature attached to the bag can sense whatever is placed inside the bag. Animal or vegetable matter placed wholly in the bag is devoured and lost forever.
