entries: You are adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52} and your second turn at your {@variantrule Initiative|SRD52} minus 10.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Sorcery
entries: {@i Breathe the Magic of Dragons}

Your innate magic comes from the gift of a dragon. Perhaps an ancient dragon facing death bequeathed some of its magical power to you or your ancestor. You might have absorbed magic from a site infused with dragons' power. Or perhaps you handled a treasure taken from a dragon's hoard that was steeped in draconic power. Or you might have a dragon for an ancestor.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Draconic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Draconic Spells
rows: {@spell Alter Self|SRD52}, {@spell Chromatic Orb|SRD52}, {@spell Command|SRD52}, {@spell Dragon's Breath|SRD52}

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Resilience
entries: The magic in your body manifests physical traits of your draconic gift. Your {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52|Hit Point} maximum increases by 3, and it increases by 1 whenever you gain another Sorcerer level.
Parts of you are also covered by dragon-like scales. While you aren't wearing armor, your base {@variantrule Armor Class|SRD52} equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Charisma modifiers.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Affinity
entries: Your draconic magic has an affinity with a damage type associated with dragons. Choose one of those types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison.
You have {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} to that damage type, and when you cast a spell that deals damage of that type, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Wings
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|SRD52}, you can cause draconic wings to appear on your back. The wings last for 1 hour or until you dismiss them (no action required). For the duration, you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|SRD52} of 60 feet.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} unless you spend 3 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Dragon Companion
entries: You can cast {@spell Summon Dragon|SRD52} without a Material component. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.
Whenever you start casting the spell, you can modify it so that it doesn't require {@status Concentration|SRD52}. If you do so, the spell's duration becomes 1 minute for that casting.

subclassFeature.name: Fiend Patron
entries: {@i Make a Deal with the Lower Planes}

Your pact draws on the Lower Planes, the realms of perdition. You might forge a bargain with a demon lord such as Demogorgon or Orcus; an archdevil such as Asmodeus; or a pit fiend, balor, yugoloth, or night hag that is especially mighty. That patron's aims are evil—the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you—and your path is defined by the extent to which you strive against those aims.

subclassFeature.name: Dark One's Blessing
entries: When you reduce an enemy to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52}, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|SRD52} equal to your Charisma modifier plus your Warlock level (minimum of 1 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|SRD52|Temporary Hit Point}). You also gain this benefit if someone else reduces an enemy within 10 feet of you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|SRD52}.

subclassFeature.name: Fiend Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Fiend Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Fiend Spells
rows: {@spell Burning Hands|SRD52}, {@spell Command|SRD52}, {@spell Scorching Ray|SRD52}, {@spell Suggestion|SRD52}

subclassFeature.name: Dark One's Own Luck
entries: You can call on your fiendish patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add {@dice 1d10} to your roll. You can do so after seeing the roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), but you can use it no more than once per roll. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}.

subclassFeature.name: Fiendish Resilience
entries: Choose one damage type, other than Force, whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|SRD52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}. You have {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Hurl Through Hell
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can try to instantly transport the target through the Lower Planes. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, or the target disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape. The target takes {@damage 8d10} Psychic damage if it isn't a Fiend, and it has the {@condition Incapacitated|SRD52} condition until the end of your next turn, when it returns to the space it previously occupied or the nearest unoccupied space.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52} unless you expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Evoker
entries: {@i Create Explosive Elemental Effects}

Your studies focus on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some Evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast armies from afar. Others use their power to protect others, while some seek their own gain.

subclassFeature.name: Evocation Savant
entries: Choose two {@filter Wizard spells from the Evocation school|spells|level=0;1;2|class=Wizard|school=V}, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Evocation school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Cantrip
entries: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Sculpt Spells
entries: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

subclassFeature.name: Empowered Evocation
entries: Whenever you cast a Wizard spell from the Evocation school, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of that spell.

subclassFeature.name: Overchannel
entries: You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot of levels 1–5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, you take {@damage 2d12} Necrotic damage for each level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|SRD52} and {@variantrule Immunity|SRD52}.
Each time you use this feature again before finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|SRD52}, the Necrotic damage per spell level increases by {@damage 1d12}.

table.name: Magic Item Values by Rarity; Magic Item Rarities and Values
footnotes: *Halve the value for a consumable item other than a Spell Scroll. The value of a Spell Scroll is double what it costs to scribe the scroll (as specified in the "Scribing Spell Scrolls" section of "Equipment").

table.name: Scribing Spell Scrolls; Spell Scroll Costs

trap.name: Collapsing Roof
trigger: A creature crosses a trip wire
entries: This trap uses a trip wire to collapse an unstable section of ceiling. The trip wire is 3 inches off the ground and stretches between two weak supports that topple when the trip wire is pulled.

The first creature that crosses the trip wire causes the supports to topple and the unstable section of ceiling to collapse. Each creature beneath the unstable section of ceiling must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Bludgeoning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Rubble from the collapse turns the trapped area into {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|SRD52}.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Search|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the trapped area and make a {@dc 11} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) check, detecting the trip wire and the unstable section of ceiling on a successful check. Once detected, the trip wire can be easily cut or avoided (no ability check required).

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: You can scale the trap for higher levels by increasing the damage and the save DC, as shown in the following table.

trap.name: Falling Net
trigger: A creature crosses a trip wire
entries: A falling net trap uses a trip wire to release a weighted, 10-foot-square {@item Net|SRD52} suspended from the ceiling. The trip wire is 3 inches off the ground and stretches between two columns or trees.

The first creature that crosses the trip wire causes the Net to fall on it. The target must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Restrained|SRD52} condition until it escapes. The target succeeds automatically if it's Huge or larger. A creature can take an action to make a {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics|SRD52}) check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach from the Net on a successful check.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Search|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the trapped area and make a {@dc 11} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) check, detecting the trip wire and the suspended Net on a successful check. Once detected, the trip wire can be easily cut or avoided (no ability check required).

entries.name: Destroy the Net
entries: Reducing the Net to 0 Hit Points frees any creature trapped in it (see the {@book Player's Handbook|SRD52} for the {@item Net|SRD52|Net's} statistics).

entries.name: Set the Trap
entries: A creature that has {@item Thieves' Tools|SRD52} and all the trap's components (including a Net) can try to set a falling net trap, doing so with a successful {@dc 13} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|SRD52}) check. Each attempt to set this trap takes 10 minutes.

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: You can scale the trap for higher levels by increasing the weight of the Net, which increases the save DC and the DC of the Strength ({@skill Athletics|SRD52}) check as follows: {@dc 12} at levels 5–10, {@dc 14} at levels 11–16, or {@dc 16} at levels 17–20.

trap.name: Fire-Casting Statue
trigger: A creature moves onto a pressure plate
entries: When a creature moves onto this trap's pressure plate for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, a nearby statue exhales a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|SRD52|Cone} of magical flame. The statue can look like anything, such as a dragon or a wizard. Each creature in the Cone must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: A {@spell Detect Magic|SRD52} spell reveals an aura of Evocation magic around the statue. As a {@action Search|SRD52} action, a creature within 5 feet of the statue can examine it and make a {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) check, detecting a tiny glyph on the statue on a successful check. Once the glyph is found, a character can take a {@action Study|SRD52} action to examine it and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|SRD52}) check, ascertaining that the glyph means "fire" on a successful check. As an action, a character can use a sharp tool to deface the glyph, which disarms the trap.

As a {@action Search|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the section of floor that forms the pressure plate and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) check, detecting the pressure plate on a successful check. Wedging an {@item Iron Spikes|SRD52|Iron Spike} or similar object under the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: You can scale the trap for higher levels by increasing the damage and the area of effect, as shown in the following table.

trap.name: Hidden Pit
trigger: A creature moves onto the pit's lid
entries: This 10-foot-deep pit has a hinged lid constructed from material identical to the surrounding floor. When a creature moves onto the lid, it swings open like a trapdoor, causing the creature to fall into the pit. The lid remains open thereafter.
A creature that falls into the pit takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Bludgeoning damage from the fall.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Study|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the section of floor that forms the pit's lid and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|SRD52}) check, detecting the pit on a successful check. Once the pit is detected, an Iron Spike or a similar object can be wedged between the pit's lid and the surrounding floor to prevent the lid from opening, thereby making it safe to cross. The cover can also be held shut using {@spell Arcane Lock|SRD52} or similar magic.

entries.name: Escape
entries: A creature needs a Climb Speed, climbing gear, or magic such as {@spell Spider Climb|SRD52} to scale the pit's smooth walls. (You can make the pit easier to escape by adding cracks in the walls big enough to serve as handholds and footholds.)

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: You can scale the trap for higher levels by increasing the pit's depth and damage, as shown in the following table.

trap.name: Poisoned Darts
trigger: A creature moves onto a pressure plate
entries: When a creature moves onto this trap's pressure plate for the first time on a turn, poisoned darts shoot from tubes embedded in the surrounding walls. The holes that house these tubes are obscured by dust and cobwebs, or skillfully hidden amid bas-reliefs, murals, or frescoes.
Each creature in the darts' path must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or be struck by {@dice 1d3} darts, taking 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Poison damage per dart.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Search|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the walls and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) check, detecting the holes on a successful check. Plugging all the holes with wax, cloth, or detritus prevents the darts from firing.

As a {@action Search|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the section of floor that forms the pressure plate and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) check, detecting the pressure plate on a successful check. Wedging an {@item Iron Spikes|SRD52|Iron Spike} or a similar object under the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: You can scale the trap for higher levels by increasing each dart's Poison damage as follows: 7 ({@dice 2d6}) at levels 5–10, 14 ({@dice 4d6}) at levels 11–16, or 24 ({@dice 7d6}) at levels 17–20.

trap.name: Poisoned Needle
trigger: A creature opens the trap's lock improperly or fails to disarm the trap
entries: A poisoned needle is hidden in a lock. When a creature opens the lock with any object other than the proper key, the needle springs out and stabs the creature. The creature makes a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Poison damage and has the {@condition Poisoned|SRD52} condition for 1 hour. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only.

entries.name: Avoid
entries: The trap doesn't trigger if the lock is opened using a {@spell Knock|SRD52} spell or similar magic.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Search|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the trapped lock and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|SRD52}) check, detecting the needle on a successful check. Once the trap is detected, a character can take an action to try to disarm the trap, doing so with a successful {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|SRD52}) check. On a failed check, the creature triggers the trap.

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: You can scale the trap for higher levels by increasing the damage and the save DC, as shown in the following table.

trap.name: Rolling Stone
trigger: A creature moves onto a pressure plate
entries: When a creature moves onto a hidden pressure plate, a 5-foot-radius orb of solid stone is released from a secret compartment and begins to roll. The stone and all creatures nearby roll Initiative; the stone gets a +8 bonus on its Initiative roll.

On its turn, the stone moves 60 feet in one direction, changing course if redirected by an obstacle. The stone can move through creatures' spaces, and creatures can move through the stone's space, treating it as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|SRD52}. Whenever the stone enters a creature's space for the first time on a turn or a creature enters the stone's space while the stone is rolling, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or take 55 ({@damage 10d10}) Bludgeoning damage and have the {@condition Prone|SRD52} condition.
The stone stops when it hits a wall or similar barrier. It can't go around corners, but creative dungeon builders incorporate curving turns into nearby passages that allow the stone to keep moving.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Study|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the section of floor that forms the pressure plate and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|SRD52}) check, deducing the pressure plate's function on a successful check. Wedging an Iron Spike or a similar object under the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.

entries.name: Destroy the Stone
entries: The stone is a Large object that has AC 17, HP 100, a {@variantrule Damage Threshold|SRD52} of 10, and {@variantrule Immunity|SRD52} to Poison and Psychic damage.

entries.name: Slow the Stone
entries: As an action, a creature can try to slow down the stone with a {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics|SRD52}) check. If the check is successful, the distance the stone moves on its turn is reduced by 15 feet. If that distance drops to 0, it stops moving and is no longer a threat.

trap.name: Spiked Pit
trigger: A creature moves onto the pit's lid
entries: A 10-foot-deep pit has a hinged lid constructed from material identical to the surrounding floor. When a creature moves onto the lid, it swings open like a trapdoor, causing the creature to fall into the pit, which has sharpened wooden or metal spikes at the bottom. The lid remains open thereafter.
A creature that falls into the pit lands at the bottom and takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Bludgeoning damage from the fall plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Piercing damage from the spikes.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Study|SRD52} action, a creature can examine the section of floor that forms the pit's lid and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|SRD52}) check, detecting the pit on a successful check. Once the hidden pit is detected, an Iron Spike or a similar object can be wedged between the pit's lid and the surrounding floor to prevent the lid from opening, thereby making it safe to cross. The cover can also be held shut using an {@spell Arcane Lock|SRD52} spell or similar magic.

entries.name: Escape
entries: A creature needs a Climb Speed, climbing gear, or magic such as a {@spell Spider Climb|SRD52} spell to scale the pit's smooth walls. You can make the pit easier to escape by adding cracks in the walls big enough to serve as handholds and footholds.

entries.name: At Higher Levels
entries: You can scale the trap for higher levels by increasing the pit's depth and damage, as shown in the following table.

variantrule.name: Ability Check
entries: An ability check is a {@variantrule D20 Test|srd52} that represents using one of the six abilities—or a specific skill associated with an ability—to overcome a challenge.

variantrule.name: Ability Score and Modifier
entries: A creature has six ability scores—Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma—each of which has a corresponding modifier. Add the modifier when you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|srd52} with the corresponding ability or when a rule asks you to do so.

variantrule.name: Action
entries: On your turn, you can take one action. Choose which action to take from those below or from the special actions provided by your features. These actions are defined elsewhere in this glossary:

variantrule.name: Advantage
entries: If you have Advantage on a {@variantrule D20 Test|srd52}, roll two d20s, and use the higher roll. A roll can't be affected by more than one Advantage, and Advantage and {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on the same roll cancel each other.

variantrule.name: Adventure
entries: An adventure is a series of {@variantrule Encounter|srd52|encounters}. A story emerges through playing them.

variantrule.name: Alignment
entries: A creature's alignment broadly describes its ethical attitudes and ideals. Alignment is a combination of two factors: one identifies morality (good, evil, or neutral), and the other describes attitudes toward order (lawful, chaotic, or neutral). These factors allow for nine possible combinations, such as Lawful Good and Neutral Evil.

variantrule.name: Ally
entries: A creature is your ally if it is a member of your adventuring party, your friend, on your side in combat, or a creature that the rules or the GM designates as your ally.

variantrule.name: Area of Effect
entries: The descriptions of many spells and other features specify that they have an area of effect, which typically has one of six shapes. These shapes are defined elsewhere in this glossary:

An area of effect has a point of origin, a location from which the effect's energy erupts. The rules for each shape specify how to position its point of origin. If all straight lines extending from the point of origin to a location in the area of effect are blocked, that location isn't included in the area of effect. To block a line, an obstruction must provide {@variantrule Cover|srd52|Total Cover}.

If the creator of an area of effect places it at an unseen point and an obstruction—such as a wall—is between the creator and that point, the point of origin comes into being on the near side of the obstruction.

variantrule.name: Armor Class
entries: An Armor Class (AC) is the target number for an attack roll. AC represents how difficult it is to hit a target.
Your base AC calculation is 10 plus your Dexterity modifier. If a rule gives you another base AC calculation, you choose which calculation to use; you can't use more than one.

variantrule.name: Armor Training
entries: Armor training allows you to use armor of a certain category without the following drawbacks. If you wear {@filter Light|items|type=Light Armor}, {@filter Medium|items|type=Medium Armor}, or {@filter Heavy|items|type=Heavy Armor} armor and lack training with it, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on any {@variantrule D20 Test|srd52} that involves Strength or Dexterity, and you can't cast spells. If you use a {@item Shield|srd52} and lack training with it, you don't gain its AC bonus.

variantrule.name: Attack Roll
entries: An attack roll is a {@variantrule D20 Test|srd52} that represents making an attack with a weapon, an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|srd52}, or a spell.

variantrule.name: Attitude
entries: A {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} has a starting attitude toward a {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player character}: {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|srd52|Friendly}, {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|srd52|Hostile}, or {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|srd52|Indifferent}.

variantrule.name: Attunement
entries: Some magic items require a creature to form a bond—called Attunement—with them before the creature can use an item's magical properties. A creature can have Attunement with no more than three magic items at a time.

variantrule.name: Bonus Action
entries: A Bonus Action is a special action that you can take on the same turn that you take an action. You can't take more than one Bonus Action on a turn, and you have a Bonus Action to take only if a rule explicitly says so.

variantrule.name: Breaking Objects
entries: Objects can be harmed by attacks and by some spells, using the rules below. If an object is exceedingly fragile, the GM may allow a creature to break it automatically with the {@action Attack|srd52} or {@action Utilize|srd52} action.

entries.name: Armor Class
entries: The Object Armor Class table suggests ACs for various substances.

entries.name: Hit Points
entries: An object is destroyed when it has 0 Hit Points. The Object Hit Points table suggests Hit Points for fragile and resilient objects that are Large or smaller. To track Hit Points for a Huge or Gargantuan object, divide it into Large or smaller sections, and track each section's Hit Points separately. The GM determines whether destroying part of an object causes the whole thing to collapse.

entries.name: Damage Types and Objects
entries: Objects have {@variantrule Immunity|srd52} to Poison and Psychic damage. The GM might decide that some {@variantrule Damage Types|srd52|damage types} are more or less effective against an object. For example, Bludgeoning damage works well for smashing things but not for cutting. Paper or cloth objects might have {@variantrule Vulnerability|srd52} to Fire damage.

entries.name: Damage Threshold
entries: Big objects, such as castle walls, often have extra resilience represented by a damage threshold. See also "{@variantrule Damage Threshold|srd52}".

entries.name: No Ability Scores
entries: An object lacks ability scores unless a rule assigns scores to the object. Without ability scores, an object can't make ability checks, and it fails all saving throws.

variantrule.name: Bright Light
entries: Bright Light is normal illumination.

variantrule.name: Burrow Speed
entries: A creature that has a Burrow Speed can use that speed to move through sand, earth, mud, or ice. The creature can't burrow through solid rock unless the creature has a trait that allows it to do so.

variantrule.name: Campaign
entries: A campaign is a series of {@variantrule Adventure|srd52|adventures}.

variantrule.name: Cantrip
entries: A cantrip is a level 0 spell, which is cast without a spell slot.

variantrule.name: Carrying Capacity
entries: Your size and Strength score determines the maximum weight in pounds that you can carry, as shown in the Carrying Capacity table. The table also shows the maximum weight you can drag, lift or push.
While dragging, lifting, or pushing weight in excess of the maximum weight you can carry, your Speed can be no more than 5 feet.

variantrule.name: Challenge Rating
entries: Challenge Rating (CR) summarizes the threat a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} poses to a group of four {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player characters}. Compare a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} CR to the characters' level. If the CR is higher, the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} is likely a danger. If the CR is lower, the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} likely poses little threat. But circumstances and the number of {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player characters} can significantly alter how threatening a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} is in actual play. "{@book Gameplay Toolbox|srd52|10}" ("Combat Encounters") provides guidance to the GM on using CR while planning potential combat {@variantrule Encounter|srd52|encounters}.

variantrule.name: Character Sheet
entries: A character sheet is a paper or digital record that you use to track your character's information.

variantrule.name: Climb Speed
entries: A Climb Speed can be used in place of {@variantrule Speed|srd52} to traverse a vertical surface without expending the extra movement normally associated with climbing.

variantrule.name: Climbing
entries: While you're climbing, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot (2 extra feet in {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|srd52|difficult terrain}). You ignore this extra cost if you have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|srd52} and use it to climb. At the GM's option, climbing a slippery surface or one with few handholds might require a successful {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|srd52}) check.

variantrule.name: Condition
entries: A condition is a temporary game state. The definition of a condition says how it affects its recipient, and various rules define how to end a condition. This glossary defines these conditions:
A condition doesn't stack with itself; a recipient either has a condition or doesn't. The {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} condition is an exception to that rule.

variantrule.name: Cone [Area of Effect]
entries: A Cone is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a point of origin in a direction its creator chooses. A Cone's width at any point along its length is equal to that point's distance from the point of origin. For example, a Cone is 15 feet wide at a point along its length that is 15 feet from the point of origin. The effect that creates a Cone specifies its maximum length.
A Cone's point of origin isn't included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

variantrule.name: Cover
entries: Cover provides a degree of protection to a target behind it. There are three degrees of cover, each of which provides a different benefit to a target: Half Cover (+2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws), Three-Quarters Cover (+5 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throws}), and Total Cover (can't be targeted directly). If behind more than one degree of cover, a target benefits only from the most protective degree.

variantrule.name: Crawling
entries: While you're crawling, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot (2 extra feet in {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|srd52|difficult terrain}).

variantrule.name: Creature
entries: Any being in the game, including {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|a player's character}, is a creature.

variantrule.name: Creature Type
entries: Every creature, including every {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player character}, has a tag in the rules that identifies the type of creature it is. Most {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player characters} are of the Humanoid type. These are the game's creature types:
The types don't have rules themselves, but some rules in the game affect creatures of certain types in different ways.

variantrule.name: Critical Hit
entries: If you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll, you score a Critical Hit, and the attack hits regardless of any modifiers or the target's AC. A Critical Hit lets you roll extra dice for the attack's damage against the target. Roll all of the attack's damage dice twice and add them together. Then add any relevant modifiers.

variantrule.name: Cube [Area of Effect]
entries: A Cube is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a point of origin located anywhere on a face of the Cube. The effect that creates a Cube specifies its size, which is the length of each side. A Cube's point of origin isn't included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

variantrule.name: Curses
entries: Some game effects curse a creature or an object. The effect that confers a curse defines what the curse does. Curses can be removed by the {@spell Remove Curse|srd52} and {@spell Greater Restoration|srd52} spells or other magic that explicitly ends curses.

variantrule.name: Cylinder [Area of Effect]
entries: A Cylinder is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a point of origin located at the center of the circular top or bottom of the Cylinder. The effect that creates a Cylinder specifies the radius of the Cylinder's base and the Cylinder's height.
A Cylinder's point of origin is included in the area of effect.

variantrule.name: D20 Test
entries: D20 Tests encompass the three main d20 rolls of the game: {@variantrule Ability Check|srd52|ability checks}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|srd52|attack rolls}, and {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throws}. If something in the game affects D20 Tests, it affects all three of these rolls. The GM determines whether a D20 Test is warranted in a given circumstance.

variantrule.name: Damage
entries: Damage represents harm that causes a creature or an object to lose {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Damage Roll
entries: A damage roll is a die roll, adjusted by any applicable modifiers, that deals damage to a target.

variantrule.name: Damage Threshold
entries: A creature or an object that has a damage threshold has {@variantrule Immunity|srd52} to all damage unless it takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, in which case it takes that entire instance of damage. Any damage that fails to meet or exceed the damage threshold is superficial and doesn't reduce {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}. For example, if an object has a damage threshold of 10, the object takes no damage if 9 damage is dealt to it, since that damage fails to exceed the threshold. If the same object is dealt 11 damage, it takes all of that damage.

variantrule.name: Damage Types
entries: Attacks and other harmful effects deal different types of damage. Damage types have no rules of their own, but other rules, such as Resistance, rely on the types. The Damage Types table offers examples to help a GM assign a type to a new effect.

variantrule.name: Darkness
entries: An area of Darkness is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Dead
entries: A dead creature has no {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} and can't regain them unless it is first revived by magic such as the {@spell Raise Dead|srd52} or {@spell Revivify|srd52} spell. When such a spell is cast, the spirit knows who is casting it and can refuse. The spirit of a dead creature has left the body and departed for the Outer Planes, and reviving the creature requires calling the spirit back.

If the creature returns to life, the revival effect determines the creature's current {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}. Unless otherwise stated, the creature returns to life with any {@variantrule Condition|srd52|conditions}, magical contagions, or curses that were affecting it at death if the durations of those effects are still ongoing. If the creature died with any {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} levels, it returns with 1 fewer level. If the creature had {@variantrule Attunement|srd52} to one or more magic items, it is no longer attuned to them.

variantrule.name: Death Saving Throw
entries: A {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player character} must make a Death Saving Throw (also called a Death Save) if they start their turn with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Difficult Terrain
entries: If a space is Difficult Terrain, every foot of movement in that space costs 1 extra foot. For example, moving 5 feet through Difficult Terrain costs 10 feet of movement. Difficult Terrain isn't cumulative; either a space is Difficult Terrain or it isn't.
A space is Difficult Terrain if the space contains any of the following or something similar:

items: A creature that isn't Tiny or your ally
Furniture that is sized for creatures of your size or larger
Heavy snow, ice, rubble, or undergrowth
Liquid that's between shin- and waist-deep
A narrow opening sized for a creature one size smaller than you
A slope of 20 degrees or more

variantrule.name: Difficulty Class
entries: A Difficulty Class (DC) is the target number for an ability check or a {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw}.

variantrule.name: Dim Light
entries: An area with Dim Light is {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Disadvantage
entries: If you have Disadvantage on a {@variantrule D20 Test|srd52}, roll two d20s and use the lower roll. A roll can't be affected by more than one Disadvantage, and {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} and Disadvantage on the same roll cancel each other.

variantrule.name: Emanation [Area of Effect]
entries: An Emanation is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a creature or an object in all directions. The effect that creates an Emanation specifies the distance it extends.
An Emanation moves with the creature or object that is its origin unless it is an instantaneous or a stationary effect.
An Emanation's origin (creature or object) isn't included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

variantrule.name: Encounter
entries: An encounter is a scene in an adventure that is part of at least one of the game's three pillars: social interaction, exploration, or combat.

variantrule.name: Enemy
entries: A creature is your enemy if it fights against you in combat, actively works to harm you, or is designated as your enemy by the rules or GM.

variantrule.name: Experience Points
entries: As they overcome challenges and complete adventures, characters earn Experience Points (XP) which are awarded by the GM. When a character's XP total crosses certain thresholds, the character's level increases.

variantrule.name: Expertise
entries: Expertise is a feature that enhances your use of a skill proficiency. When you make an ability check with a skill proficiency in which you have Expertise, your {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus} is doubled for that check unless the bonus is doubled by another feature.
If you gain Expertise, you gain it in one {@variantrule skill|srd52} in which you have proficiency. You can't have Expertise in the same skill proficiency more than once.

variantrule.name: Fly Speed
entries: A Fly Speed can be used to travel through the air. While you have a Fly Speed, you can stay aloft until you land, fall, or die.

variantrule.name: Flying
entries: A variety of effects allow a creature to fly. While flying, you fall if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} or {@condition Prone|srd52} condition or your {@variantrule Fly Speed|srd52} is reduced to 0. You can stay aloft in those circumstances if you can hover.

variantrule.name: Friendly [Attitude]
entries: A Friendly creature views you favorably. You have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52|advantage} on an ability check to influence a Friendly creature.

variantrule.name: Grappling
entries: A creature can grapple another creature. Characters typically grapple by using an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|srd52}. Many {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monsters} have special attacks that allow them to quickly grapple prey. However a grapple is initiated, it follows these rules.

entries.name: Grappled Condition
entries: Successfully grappling a creature gives it the {@condition Grappled|srd52} condition.

entries.name: One Grapple per Hand
entries: A creature must have a hand free to grapple another creature. Some stat blocks and game effects allow a creature to grapple using a tentacle, a maw, or another body part. Whatever part a grappler uses, it can grapple only one creature at a time with that part, and the grappler can't use that part to target another creature unless it ends the grapple.

entries.name: Ending a Grapple
entries: A Grappled creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|srd52}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|srd52}) check against the grapple's escape DC, ending the {@variantrule Condition|srd52|condition} on itself on a success. The {@variantrule Condition|srd52|condition} also ends if the grappler has the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} condition or if the distance between the Grappled target and the grappler exceeds the grapple's range. In addition, the grappler can release the target at any time (no action required).

variantrule.name: Hazard
entries: A {@5etools hazard|trapshazards.html} is an environmental danger.

variantrule.name: Healing
entries: Healing is how you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Heavily Obscured
entries: You have the {@condition Blinded|srd52} condition while trying to see something in a Heavily Obscured space.

variantrule.name: Heroic Inspiration
entries: If you ({@variantrule Player Character|srd52|a player character}) have Heroic Inspiration, you can expend it to reroll any die immediately after rolling it, and you must use the new roll.
If you gain Heroic Inspiration but already have it, it's lost unless you give it to a {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player character} who lacks it.

variantrule.name: High Jump
entries: When you make a High Jump, you leap into the air a number of feet equal to 3 plus your Strength modifier (minimum of 0 feet) if you move at least 10 feet on foot immediately before the jump. When you make a standing High Jump, you can jump only half that distance. Either way, each foot of the jump costs a foot of movement.
You can extend your arms half your height above yourself during the jump. Thus, you can reach a distance equal to the height of the jump plus 1½ times your height.

variantrule.name: Hit Point Dice
entries: Hit Point Dice, or Hit Dice for short, help determine a {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player character's} Hit Point maximum, as explained in {@book Character Creation|srd52|2}. Most {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monsters} also have Hit Dice. A creature can spend Hit Dice during a {@variantrule Short Rest|srd52} to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Hit Points
entries: Hit Points (HP) are a measure of how difficult it is to kill or destroy a creature or an object. Damage reduces Hit Points, and healing restores them. You can't have more Hit Points than your Hit Point maximum, and you can't have less than 0.

variantrule.name: Hostile [Attitude]
entries: A Hostile creature views you unfavorably. You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on an ability check to influence a Hostile creature.

variantrule.name: Hover
entries: Some creatures can hover, as noted in their stat blocks, and some spells and other effects grant the ability to hover. Hovering while {@variantrule Flying|srd52|flying} prevents you from falling in certain circumstances.

variantrule.name: Illusions
entries: Spells and other effects sometimes create magical illusions. Such an effect defines what the illusion does and which senses or mental faculties it deceives.

If an illusion manifests in space, the illusion is insubstantial and weightless, yet it seems to be affected by the environment as if the illusion were real unless the effect that created it specifies otherwise. For example, a visual illusion of a creature casts shadows and reflections, and wind appears to affect the illusory creature. Similarly, an audible illusion echoes in an echoey space.

variantrule.name: Immunity
entries: If you have Immunity to a {@variantrule Damage Types|srd52|damage type} or a {@variantrule Condition|srd52|condition}, it doesn't affect you in any way.

variantrule.name: Improvised Weapons
entries: An improvised weapon is an object wielded as a makeshift weapon, such as broken glass, a table leg, or a frying pan. A Simple or Martial weapon also counts as an improvised weapon if it's wielded in a way contrary to its design; if you use a Ranged weapon to make a melee attack or throw a Melee weapon that lacks the Thrown property, the weapon counts as an improvised weapon. An improvised weapon follows the rules below.

entries.name: Proficiency
entries: Don't add your {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus} to attack rolls with an improvised weapon.

entries.name: Damage
entries: On a hit, the weapon deals {@damage 1d4} damage of a type the GM thinks is appropriate for the object.

entries.name: Range
entries: If you throw the weapon, it has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Weapon Equivalents
entries: If an improvised weapon resembles a Simple or Martial weapon, the GM may say it functions as that weapon and uses that weapon's rules. For example, the GM could treat a table leg as a {@item Club|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Indifferent [Attitude]
entries: An Indifferent creature has no desire to help or hinder you. Indifferent is the default attitude of a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster}.

variantrule.name: Initiative
entries: Initiative determines the order of turns during combat. The combat rules in {@book Playing the Game|srd52|1} explain how to roll Initiative.

Sometimes a GM might have combatants use their Initiative scores instead of rolling Initiative. Your Initiative score equals 10 plus your Dexterity modifier. If you have {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} on Initiative rolls, increase your Initiative score by 5. If you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on those rolls, decrease that score by 5.

variantrule.name: Jumping
entries: When you jump, you make either a {@variantrule Long Jump|srd52} (horizontal) or a {@variantrule High Jump|srd52} (vertical).

variantrule.name: Knocking Out a Creature
entries: When you would reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} with a melee attack, you can instead reduce the creature to 1 Hit Point. The creature then has the {@condition Unconscious|srd52} condition and starts a {@variantrule Short Rest|srd52}.

The creature remains Unconscious until it regains any {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} or until someone uses an action to administer first aid to it, which requires a successful {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|srd52}) check.

variantrule.name: Lightly Obscured
entries: You have {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|srd52}) checks to see something in a Lightly Obscured space.

variantrule.name: Line [Area of Effect]
entries: A Line is an area of effect that extends from a point of origin in a straight path along its length and covers an area defined by its width. The effect that creates a Line specifies its length and width.
A Line's point of origin isn't included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

variantrule.name: Long Jump
entries: When you make a Long Jump, you leap horizontally a number of feet up to your Strength score if you move at least 10 feet immediately before the jump. When you make a standing Long Jump, you can leap only half that distance. Either way, each foot you jump costs a foot of movement.
If you land in {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|srd52|difficult terrain}, you must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|srd52}) check or have the {@condition Prone|srd52} condition.

This Long Jump rule assumes that the height of the jump doesn't matter, such as a jump across a stream or chasm. At your GM's option, you must succeed on a {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics|srd52}) check to clear a low obstacle (no taller than a quarter of the jump's distance), such as a hedge or low wall. Otherwise, you hit the obstacle.

variantrule.name: Long Rest
entries: A Long Rest is a period of extended downtime—at least 8 hours—available to any creature. During a Long Rest, you sleep for at least 6 hours and perform no more than 2 hours of light activity, such as reading, talking, eating, or standing watch.
During sleep, you have the {@condition Unconscious|srd52} condition. After you finish a Long Rest, you must wait at least 16 hours before starting another one.

entries.name: Benefits of the Rest
entries: To start a Long Rest, you must have at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52|Hit Point}. When you finish the rest, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Regain All HP
entries: You regain all lost {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} and all spent {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|srd52}. If your Hit Point maximum was reduced, it returns to normal.

items.name: Ability Scores Restored
entries: If any of your ability scores were reduced, they return to normal.

items.name: Exhaustion Reduced
entries: If you have the {@condition Exhaustion|srd52} condition, its level decreases by 1.

items.name: Special Feature
entries: Some features are recharged by a Long Rest. If you have such a feature, it recharges in the way specified in its description.

entries.name: Interrupting the Rest
entries: A Long Rest is stopped by the following interruptions:

items: Casting a spell other than a cantrip
1 hour of walking or other physical exertion.

entries: If you rested at least 1 hour before the interruption you gain the benefits of a {@variantrule Short Rest|srd52}.
You can resume a Long Rest immediately after an interruption. If you do so, the rest requires 1 additional hour per interruption to finish.

variantrule.name: Magical Effect
entries: An effect is magical if it is created by a spell, a magic item, or a phenomenon that a rule labels as magical.

variantrule.name: Monster
entries: A monster is a creature controlled by the GM, even if the creature is benevolent.

variantrule.name: Nonplayer Character
entries: A nonplayer character (NPC) is a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} that has a personal name and a distinct personality.

variantrule.name: Object
entries: An object is a nonliving, distinct thing. Composite things, like buildings, comprise more than one object.

variantrule.name: Occupied Space
entries: A space is occupied if a creature is in it or if it is completely filled by objects.

variantrule.name: Passive Perception
entries: Passive Perception is a score that reflects a creature's general awareness of its surroundings. The GM uses this score when determining whether a creature notices something without consciously making a Wisdom ({@skill Perception|srd52}) check.

A creature's Passive Perception equals 10 plus the creature's Wisdom ({@skill Perception|srd52}) check bonus. If the creature has {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} on such checks, increase the score by 5. If the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|srd52} on them, decrease the score by 5. For example, a level 1 character with a Wisdom of 15 and proficiency in Perception has a Passive Perception of 14 ({@dice 10 + 2 + 2}). If that character has {@variantrule Advantage|srd52} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|srd52}) checks, the score becomes {@dice 10 + 2 + 2 + 5|19}.

variantrule.name: Per Day
entries: If a rule says you can use something a certain number of times per day, that means you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|srd52} to use it again after you run out of uses.

variantrule.name: Player Character
entries: A player character is a character controlled by a {@link player|https://coveryourtracks.eff.org}.

variantrule.name: Possession
entries: Some effects cause a creature to be possessed by another creature or entity. A possessing effect defines how the possession operates. Possession can be prevented by the {@spell Protection from Evil and Good|srd52} spell and ended by the {@spell Dispel Evil and Good|srd52} spell.

variantrule.name: Proficiency
entries: If you have proficiency with something, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to any {@variantrule D20 Test|srd52} you make using that thing. A creature might have proficiency in a skill or {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} or with a weapon or tool.

variantrule.name: Reaction
entries: A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction's description. You can take a Reaction on another creature's turn, and if you take it on your turn, you can do so even if you also take an action, a {@variantrule Bonus Action|srd52}, or both. Once you take a Reaction, you can't take another one until the start of your next turn. The {@action Opportunity Attack|srd52} is a Reaction available to all creatures.

variantrule.name: Resistance
entries: If you have Resistance to a {@variantrule Damage Types|srd52|damage type}, damage of that type is halved against you (round down). Resistance is applied only once to an instance of damage.

variantrule.name: Ritual
entries: If you have a spell prepared that has the Ritual tag, you can cast that spell as a Ritual. The Ritual version of a spell takes 10 minutes longer to cast than normal. It also doesn't expend a spell slot, which means the ritual version of a spell can't be cast at a higher level.

variantrule.name: Round Down
entries: Whenever you divide or multiply a number in the game, round down if you end up with a fraction, even if the fraction is one-half or greater. Some rules make an exception and tell you to round up.

variantrule.name: Save
entries: Save is another name for a {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw}.

variantrule.name: Saving Throw
entries: A saving throw—also called a save—represents an attempt to avoid or resist a threat. You normally make a saving throw only when a rule requires you to do so, but you can decide to fail the save without rolling. The result of a save is detailed in the effect that allowed it. If a target is forced to make a save and lacks the ability score used by it, the target automatically fails.

variantrule.name: Shape-Shifting
entries: If an effect, such as Wild Shape or the {@spell Polymorph|srd52} spell, lets you shape-shift, its description specifies what happens to you. Unless that description says otherwise, any ongoing effects on you—{@variantrule Condition|srd52|conditions}, spells, curses, and the like—carry over from one form to the other. You revert to your true form if you die.

variantrule.name: Short Rest
entries: A Short Rest is a 1-hour period of downtime, during which a creature does nothing more strenuous than reading, talking, eating, or standing watch. To start a Short Rest, you must have at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52|Hit Point}.

entries.name: Benefits of the Rest
entries: When you finish the rest, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Spend Hit Point Dice
entries: You can spend one or more of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|srd52} to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}. For each {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|srd52|Hit Point Die} you spend in this way, roll the die and add your Constitution modifier to it. You regain {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} equal to the total (minimum of 1 Hit Point). You can decide to spend an additional {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|srd52|Hit Point Die} after each roll.

items.name: Special Feature
entries: Some features are recharged by a Short Rest. If you have such a feature, it recharges in the way specified in its description.

entries.name: Interrupting the Rest
entries: A Short Rest is stopped by the following interruptions:

items: Casting a spell other than a cantrip

entries: An interrupted Short Rest confers no benefits.

variantrule.name: Simultaneous Effects
entries: If two or more things happen at the same time on a turn, the person at the game table—player or GM whose turn it is decides the order in which those things happen. For example, if two effects occur at the start of a {@variantrule Player Character|srd52|player character's} turn, the player decides which of the effects happens first.

variantrule.name: Size
entries: A creature or an object belongs to a size category: Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. A creature's size determines how much space the creature occupies in combat. An object's size affects its {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Skill
entries: A skill is an {@book area of specialization|srd52|1|Skill List} associated with an ability check. If you have proficiency in a skill, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus} when you make an ability check associated with that skill.

variantrule.name: Speed
entries: A creature has a Speed, which is the distance in feet the creature can cover when it moves on its turn.

entries.name: Special Speeds
entries: Some creatures have special speeds, such as a {@variantrule Burrow Speed|srd52}, {@variantrule Climb Speed|srd52}, {@variantrule Fly Speed|srd52}, or {@variantrule Swim Speed|srd52}, each of which is defined in this glossary. If you have more than one speed, choose which one to use when you move; you can switch between the speeds during your move. Whenever you switch, subtract the distance already moved from the new speed. The result determines how much farther you can move. If the result is 0 or less, you can't use the new speed during the current move. For example, if you have a Speed of 30 and a {@variantrule Fly Speed|srd52} of 40, you could fly 10 feet, walk 10 feet, and leap into the air to fly 20 feet more.

entries.name: Changes to Your Speeds
entries: If an effect increases or decreases your Speed for a time, any special speed you have increases or decreases by an equal amount for the same duration. For example, if your Speed is reduced to 0 and you have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|srd52}, your {@variantrule Climb Speed|srd52} is also reduced to 0. Similarly, if your Speed is halved and you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|srd52}, your {@variantrule Fly Speed|srd52} is also halved.

variantrule.name: Spell
entries: A spell is a {@variantrule Magical Effect|srd52|magical effect} that has the characteristics described in {@book Spells|srd52|7}.

variantrule.name: Spell Attack
entries: A spell attack is an attack roll made as part of a spell or another {@variantrule Magical Effect|srd52|magical effect}.

variantrule.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: A Spellcasting Focus is an object that certain creatures can use in place of a spell's Material components if those materials aren't consumed by the spell and don't have a cost specified. Some classes allow its members to use certain types of Spellcasting Focuses.

variantrule.name: Sphere [Area of Effect]
entries: A Sphere is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a point of origin outward in all directions. The effect that creates a Sphere specifies the distance it extends as the radius of the Sphere.
A Sphere's point of origin is included in the Sphere's area of effect.

variantrule.name: Stable
entries: A creature is Stable if it has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} but isn't required to make {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|srd52|Death Saving Throws}.

variantrule.name: Stat Block
entries: A stat block contains the game statistics of a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster}. Each stat block includes the following information presented after the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} name.

entries.name: Size
entries: A {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} is Tiny, Small, Med ium, Large, Huge, or Gargantuan.

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: This entry notes the family of beings a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} belongs to, along with any descriptive tags.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: An alignment is suggested for the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster}, with the GM determining its actual alignment.

entries.name: AC, Initiative, and HP
entries: These entries give the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} {@variantrule Armor Class|srd52}, {@variantrule Initiative|srd52}, and {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}, which are detailed in {@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}. In parentheses after the {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}, the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|srd52} are provided, along with the contribution of its Constitution, if any, to its {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}. Following the {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} modifier is an {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} score. Some creatures that are created by magic lack Hit Dice and {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} information.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Here the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} Speed is provided, along with any special speeds.

entries.name: Ability Scores
entries: A table provides the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} ability scores, modifiers, and {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} modifiers, all of which are detailed in {@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}.

entries.name: Skills
entries: This entry lists the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} skill proficiencies, if any.

entries.name: Resistances and Vulnerabilities
entries: These entries list the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} Resistances and Vulnerabilities, if any.

entries.name: Immunities
entries: This section lists the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} damage and {@variantrule Condition|srd52|condition} Immunities, if any.

entries.name: Gear
entries: If the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} has any equipment that can be given away or retrieved, it's listed in this entry.

entries.name: Senses
entries: This entry lists the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} special senses, such as {@sense Darkvision|srd52}, and its Passive {@skill Perception|srd52}.

entries.name: Languages
entries: This entry lists any languages the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} knows.

entries.name: CR
entries: Challenge Rating summarizes the threat a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} poses and is detailed in the {@book Monster Manual|srd52}. The Experience Points characters receive for defeating a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} and its {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus} follow. Some creatures that are created by magic have no CR.

entries.name: Traits
entries: The {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} traits, if any, are features that are active at all times or in certain situations.

entries.name: Actions
entries: The {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} can take these actions in addition to those detailed in this glossary.

entries.name: Bonus Actions
entries: If the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} has {@variantrule Bonus Action|srd52} options, they are listed in this section.

entries.name: Reactions
entries: If the {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster} can take special {@variantrule Reaction|srd52|Reactions}, those are listed in this section.

entries.name: Attack Notation
entries: The entry for a {@variantrule Monster|srd52|monster's} attack starts by identifying whether the attack is a melee or a ranged attack and then provides the attack roll's bonus, its reach or range, and what happens on a hit. An attack is against one target unless its entry says otherwise.

entries.name: Saving Throw Effect Notation
entries: If an effect forces a {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw}, the effect's entry starts by identifying the kind of {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} required and then provides the save's DC, a description of which creatures must make the save, and what happens on a failed or a successful save.

entries.name: Damage Notation
entries: A stat block usually provides both a static number and a die expression for each instance of damage. For example, an attack might deal 4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) damage on a hit. The GM determines whether you use the static number or the die expression in parentheses; you don't use both.

variantrule.name: Swim Speed
entries: A Swim Speed can be used to swim without expending the extra movement normally associated with swimming.

variantrule.name: Swimming
entries: While you're swimming, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot (2 extra feet in {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|srd52|difficult terrain}). You ignore this extra cost if you have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|srd52} and use it to swim. At the GM's option, moving any distance in rough water might require a successful {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|srd52}) check.

variantrule.name: Target
entries: A target is the creature or object targeted by an attack roll, forced to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} by an effect, or selected to receive the effects of a spell or another phenomenon.

variantrule.name: Telepathy
entries: Telepathy is a magical ability that allows a creature to communicate mentally with another creature within a specified range. Unless a rule states otherwise, the contacted creature doesn't need to share a language with the telepath to understand this communication, but the contacted creature must be able to understand at least one language or be telepathic itself to understand.

A telepath doesn't need to see a contacted creature, and the telepath can start or end the telepathic contact at any time (no action required). Telepathic contact can't be initiated and is immediately broken if either the telepath or the other creature has the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} condition. Telepathic contact is also broken if the contacted creature is no longer within the telepathy's range or if the telepath contacts a different creature within range.

A creature without telepathy can receive telepathic messages but can't initiate a telepathic conversation. Once a telepathic conversation starts, the non-telepath can communicate mentally to the telepath until the telepathic connection ends.

variantrule.name: Teleportation
entries: Teleportation is a special kind of magical transportation. If you teleport, you disappear and reappear elsewhere instantly, without moving through the intervening space. This transportation doesn't expend movement unless a rule tells you otherwise, and teleportation never provokes {@action Opportunity Attack|srd52|Opportunity Attacks}.

When you teleport, all the equipment you're wearing and carrying teleports with you. If you're touching another creature when you teleport, that creature doesn't teleport with you unless the teleportation effect says otherwise.
If the destination space of your teleportation is occupied by another creature or blocked by a solid obstacle, you instead appear in the nearest unoccupied space of your choice.
The description of a teleportation effect tells you if you must see the teleportation's destination.

variantrule.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: Temporary Hit Points are granted by certain effects and act as a buffer against losing real {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}.

variantrule.name: Unarmed Strike
entries: Instead of using a weapon to make a melee attack, you can use a punch, kick, head-butt, or similar forceful blow. In game terms, this is an Unarmed Strike—a melee attack that involves you using your body to damage, grapple, or shove a target within 5 feet of you.
Whenever you use your Unarmed Strike, choose one of the following options for its effect.

entries.name: Damage
entries: You make an attack roll against the target. Your bonus to the roll equals your Strength modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus}. On a hit, the target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to 1 plus your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Grapple
entries: The target must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} (it chooses which), or it has the {@condition Grappled|srd52} condition. The DC for the {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} and any escape attempts equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus}. This grapple is possible only if the target is no more than one size larger than you and if you have a hand free to grab it.

entries.name: Shove
entries: The target must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} (it chooses which), or you either push it 5 feet away or cause it to have the {@condition Prone|srd52} condition. The DC for the {@variantrule Saving Throw|srd52|saving throw} equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus}. This shove is possible only if the target is no more than one size larger than you.

variantrule.name: Unoccupied Space
entries: A space is unoccupied if no creatures are in it and it isn't completely filled by objects.

variantrule.name: Vulnerability
entries: If you have Vulnerability to a {@variantrule Damage Types|srd52|damage type}, damage of that type is doubled against you. Vulnerability is applied only once to an instance of damage.

variantrule.name: Weapon
entries: A weapon is an object that is in the {@filter Simple|items|category=basic|type=simple weapon} or {@filter Martial|items|category=basic|type=martial weapon} weapon category.

variantrule.name: Weapon Attack
entries: A weapon attack is an attack roll made with a weapon.

vehicle.name: Apparatus of the Crab

swim.condition: (or 0 ft. for both if the legs aren't extended)

entries: This item first appears to be a sealed iron barrel weighing 500 pounds. The barrel has a hidden catch, which can be found with a successful {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|srd52}) check. Releasing the catch unlocks a hatch at one end of the barrel, allowing two Medium or smaller creatures to crawl inside. Ten levers are set in a row at the far end, each in a neutral position, able to move up or down. When certain levers are used, the apparatus transforms to resemble a giant lobster.

To be used as a vehicle, the apparatus requires one pilot. While the apparatus's hatch is closed, the compartment is airtight and watertight. The compartment holds enough air for 10 hours of breathing, divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.
The apparatus floats on water. It can also go underwater to a depth of 900 feet. Below that, the vehicle takes {@damage 2d6} Bludgeoning damage each minute from pressure.

A creature in the compartment can take a {@action Utilize|srd52} action to move as many as two of the apparatus's levers up or down. After each use, a lever goes back to its neutral position. Each lever, from left to right, functions as shown in the Apparatus of the Crab Levers table.

entries.caption: Apparatus of the Crab Levers
rows: Legs extend, allowing the apparatus to walk and swim.
Legs retract, reducing the apparatus's {@variantrule Speed|srd52} and {@variantrule Swim Speed|srd52} to 0 and making it unable to benefit from bonuses to speed.
Side window shutters open (two per side).
Side window shutters close (two per side).
Two claws extend from the front side of the apparatus.
Each extended claw makes the following melee attack: {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d6}) Bludgeoning damage.
Each extended claw makes the following melee attack: {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft. {@h}The target has the {@condition Grappled|srd52} condition (escape {@dc 15}).
The apparatus walks or swims forward provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus walks or swims backward provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus turns 90 degrees counterclockwise provided its legs are extended.
The apparatus turns 90 degrees clockwise provided its legs are extended.
Eyelike fixtures emit {@variantrule Bright Light|srd52} in a 30-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|srd52} for an additional 30 feet.
The apparatus sinks up to 20 feet if it's in liquid.
The apparatus rises up to 20 feet if it's in liquid.
The rear hatch unseals and opens.
The rear hatch closes and seals.
